sentences.zh: 【唐紀三十六】　起強圍作噩九月，盡著雍閹茂，凡一年有奇。

translations.literal: [Tang Annals 36] Beginning in the ninth month of the year Qiangwei Zuo'e, ending in Zhuyong Yanmao, altogether a year and a fraction.
translations.idiomatic: [Tang Annals, Part 36] From the ninth month of 757 through 758, covering somewhat more than one year.

sentences.zh: 肅宗文明武德大聖大宣孝皇帝中之下至德二年（

translations.literal: The latter part of the middle section of Emperor Suzong the Civil, Cultured, Martial, Virtuous, Great Sage, Great Proclaimer of Filial Piety, in the second year of Zhide (
translations.idiomatic: In the latter portion of the reign of Emperor Suzong, second year of Zhide (

sentences.zh: 丁酉，公元七五七年）

translations.literal: dingyou, corresponding to the year 757 CE)
translations.idiomatic: dingyou, 757 CE)

sentences.zh: 九月，丁丑，希德以輕騎至城下挑戰。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on day dingchou, Xide led light cavalry to the foot of the walls to challenge battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on dingchou, Cai Xide rode up before the walls with a light detachment to offer battle.

sentences.zh: 千里帥百騎開門突出，欲擒之；

translations.literal: Qianli led a hundred horsemen, opened the gate and burst out, intending to capture him;
translations.idiomatic: Lei Qianli led a hundred horsemen out through the opened gate in a sudden charge, hoping to seize him;

sentences.zh: 會救至，千里收騎退還，橋壞，墜塹中，反為希德所擒。

translations.literal: Just then rescue arrived; Qianli gathered his horsemen and withdrew, but the bridge broke and he fell into the moat, and was instead captured by Xide.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel reinforcements then arrived; Qianli wheeled his men back, but the bridge gave way and he plunged into the ditch, where Cai Xide captured him instead.

sentences.zh: 仰謂從騎曰：「吾不幸至此，天也！

translations.literal: Looking up he said to the horsemen who followed him: "That I have unluckily come to this pass is Heaven's doing!
translations.idiomatic: He looked up and told his escort: "That I have come to this pass is Heaven's will!

sentences.zh: 歸語諸將，善為守備，寧失帥，不可失城。

translations.literal: Go back and tell the generals to keep the defenses well; better to lose a commander than to lose the city.
translations.idiomatic: Go back and tell the generals to hold the defenses firm: better to lose a commander than to lose the city.

sentences.zh: 」希德攻城，竟不克，送千里於洛陽，安慶緒以為特進，囚之客省。

translations.literal: " Xide attacked the city but in the end could not take it; he sent Qianli to Luoyang, and An Qingxu made him Supernumerary Senior Grand Master and imprisoned him in the Guest Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: " Cai Xide pressed the siege but could not take the city. He sent Qianli to Luoyang, where An Qingxu gave him the honorary rank of tejin and kept him confined in the Guest Bureau.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀以回紇兵精，勸上益征其兵以擊賊。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi, because the Uyghur troops were elite, urged the emperor to recruit more of their forces to strike the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi, impressed by the quality of the Uyghur troops, urged the emperor to summon more of them for the campaign against the rebels.

sentences.zh: 懷仁可汗遣其子葉護及將軍帝德等將精兵四千餘人來至鳳翔。

translations.literal: Qaghan Yaoluoshan sent his son Yabgu and the generals Dide and others to lead more than four thousand elite troops to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: The Qaghan Yaoluoshan sent his son Yabgu, along with Generals Dide and others, with more than four thousand picked troops to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 上引見葉護，宴勞賜賚，惟其所欲。

translations.literal: The emperor received Yabgu in audience, feasted and rewarded him, granting whatever he desired.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor received Yabgu in audience, entertained him at a feast, and lavished gifts on him, granting whatever he asked.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，元帥廣平王俶將朔方等軍及回紇、西域之眾十五萬，號二十萬，發鳳翔。

translations.literal: On day dinghai, the commander-in-chief, the Prince of Guangping Li Chu, led the Shuofang armies and the Uyghur and Western Regions forces—one hundred fifty thousand in all, proclaimed as two hundred thousand—and set out from Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, the supreme commander, Prince of Guangping Li Chu, marched from Fengxiang at the head of the Shuofang armies and Uyghur and Western Region allies—150,000 men in all, though the army was announced as 200,000.

sentences.zh: 俶見葉護，約為兄弟，葉護大喜，謂俶為兄。

translations.literal: Chu met Yabgu and pledged brotherhood; Yabgu was greatly pleased and addressed Chu as elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: When Chu met Yabgu, they swore brotherhood; Yabgu was delighted and called Chu his elder brother.

sentences.zh: 回紇至扶風，郭子儀留宴三日。

translations.literal: When the Uyghurs reached Fufeng, Guo Ziyi detained them for a three-day feast.
translations.idiomatic: When the Uyghurs reached Fufeng, Guo Ziyi held them for a three-day feast.

sentences.zh: 葉護曰：「國家有急，遠來相助，何以食為！

translations.literal: Yabgu said: "The state is in peril and we have come from afar to help—what need is there for feasting!
translations.idiomatic: Yabgu said: "Your realm is in peril and we have come from afar to help—what time is there for feasting!

sentences.zh: 」宴畢，即行。

translations.literal: " When the feast ended, they set out at once.
translations.idiomatic: " As soon as the feast ended, they marched on.

sentences.zh: 日給其軍羊二百口，牛二十頭，米四十斛。

translations.literal: Each day his army was supplied with two hundred sheep, twenty head of cattle, and forty hu of grain.
translations.idiomatic: Each day his troops were rationed two hundred sheep, twenty cattle, and forty hu of grain.

sentences.zh: 庚子，諸軍俱發；

translations.literal: On day gengzi, all the armies set out together;
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi, the allied armies marched out together;

sentences.zh: 壬寅，至長安城西，陳於香積寺北澧水之東。

translations.literal: on day renyin they reached the west of Chang'an and formed battle lines east of the Li River north of Xiangji Temple.
translations.idiomatic: and on renyin they reached the western approaches to Chang'an and drew up east of the Li River, north of Xiangji Temple.

sentences.zh: 李嗣業為前軍，郭子儀為中軍，王思禮為後軍。

translations.literal: Li Siye commanded the vanguard, Guo Ziyi the center, and Wang Simo the rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siye led the vanguard, Guo Ziyi the center, and Wang Simo the rear.

sentences.zh: 賊眾十萬陳於其北，李歸仁出挑戰，官軍逐之，逼於其陳。

translations.literal: A hundred thousand rebel troops were arrayed to their north; Li Guiren came out to challenge, and the government army pursued him, pressing close to the rebel formation.
translations.idiomatic: A hundred thousand rebels stood ranged to the north. Li Guiren rode out to challenge battle, and the imperial forces chased him back against the rebel line.

sentences.zh: 賊軍齊進，官軍卻，為賊所乘，軍中驚亂，賊爭趣輜重。

translations.literal: The rebel army advanced together; the government army fell back and was taken advantage of by the rebels; the army was thrown into alarm and disorder, and the rebels all rushed for the baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels advanced in a body; the imperial line gave ground and was overrun. Panic spread through the ranks as the rebels surged toward the baggage train.

sentences.zh: 李嗣業曰：「今日不以身餌賊，軍無孑遺矣。

translations.literal: Li Siye said: "If today I do not offer my body as bait to the rebels, the army will not have a single survivor left.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siye cried: "Unless I throw my life before the rebels today, not a man of this army will walk away alive.

sentences.zh: 」乃肉袒，執長刀，立於陣前，大呼奮擊，當其刀者，人馬俱碎，殺數十人，陣乃稍定。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he bared his torso, grasped a long blade, and stood before the formation, shouting as he struck fiercely; those who met his blade, man and horse alike, were shattered; he killed several tens of men, and the formation was then somewhat steadied.
translations.idiomatic: " He stripped to the waist, seized a long saber, and planted himself before the line, roaring as he hacked his way forward. Man and horse alike shattered before his blade; he cut down dozens, and the formation at last held.

sentences.zh: 於是嗣業帥前軍各執長刀，如牆而進，身先士卒，所向摧靡。

translations.literal: Thereupon Siye led the vanguard, each man grasping a long blade, advancing like a wall; he went before the soldiers, and wherever he turned, the enemy was shattered.
translations.idiomatic: Siye then led the vanguard forward with long blades in hand, advancing like a moving wall. He took the lead himself, and wherever he turned, the enemy line broke.

sentences.zh: 都知兵馬使王難得救其裨將，賊射之中眉，皮垂鄣目。

translations.literal: The army controller Wang Nande rescued his deputy commander; the rebels shot him in the brow, and the skin hung down, screening his eyes.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Nande, controller of army and horse, went to rescue his deputy; a rebel arrow struck him between the brows, and the flap of skin hung down over his eyes.

sentences.zh: 難得自拔箭，掣去其皮，血流被面，前戰不已。

translations.literal: Nande himself pulled out the arrow, tore off the skin, blood covering his face, and fought on ahead without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Nande pulled out the arrow himself, ripped away the hanging skin, blood streaming over his face, and fought on without pause.

sentences.zh: 賊伏精騎於陣東，欲襲官軍之後，偵者知之，朔方左廂兵馬使僕固懷恩引回紇就擊之，翦滅殆盡，賊由是氣索。

translations.literal: The rebels had hidden elite cavalry east of the formation, intending to strike the government army from the rear; scouts learned of it, and Pugu Huai'en of the Shuofang Left Wing led the Uyghurs to attack them and nearly exterminated them; the rebels' spirit was thereby broken.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels had hidden picked cavalry east of their line to take the imperial army in the rear, but scouts discovered them. Pugu Huai'en of the Shuofang Left Wing led the Uyghurs against them and cut them down almost to a man, and the rebels' fighting spirit collapsed.

sentences.zh: 李嗣業又與回紇出賊陣後，與大軍交擊，自午及酉，斬首六萬級，填溝塹死者甚眾，賊遂大潰。

translations.literal: Li Siye again, with the Uyghurs, went out behind the rebel formation and joined the main army in mutual attack; from noon until the hour of you they cut off sixty thousand heads; those who filled the ditches and moats in death were very numerous, and the rebels then broke in great rout.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siye and the Uyghurs circled behind the rebel line and struck together with the main army. From noon until evening they took sixty thousand heads; corpses choked the ditches and moats, and the rebels broke and fled in utter rout.

sentences.zh: 餘眾走入城，迨夜，囂聲不止。

translations.literal: The remaining troops fled into the city; by nightfall the clamor did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: The survivors poured into the city, and through the night the uproar never stopped.

sentences.zh: 僕固懷恩言於廣平王俶曰：「賊棄城走矣，請以二百騎追之，縛取安守忠、李歸仁等。

translations.literal: Pugu Huai'en said to the Prince of Guangping Li Chu: "The rebels have abandoned the city and fled; please let me take two hundred horsemen in pursuit and bind and capture An Shouzhong, Li Guiren, and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Pugu Huai'en told Prince of Guangping Li Chu: "The rebels have abandoned the city and fled. Give me two hundred horsemen to run them down and bring back An Shouzhong, Li Guiren, and the rest in bonds.

sentences.zh: 」俶曰：「將軍戰亦疲矣，且休息，俟明日圖之。

translations.literal: " Chu said: "General, you too are weary from battle; rest for now and we shall plan it tomorrow.
translations.idiomatic: " Chu replied: "You are exhausted from the fight, General. Rest tonight, and we will plan tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」懷恩曰：「歸仁、守忠，賊之驍將，驟勝而敗，此天賜我也，奈何縱之！

translations.literal: " Huai'en said: "Guiren and Shouzhong are the rebels' fiercest generals; having suddenly won and then lost, this is Heaven's gift to us—how can we let them go!
translations.idiomatic: " Huai'en urged: "Guiren and Shouzhong are the rebels' boldest commanders. To win a great victory and then lose them—this is a gift from Heaven! How can we let them slip away?

sentences.zh: 使復得眾，還為我患，悔之無及！

translations.literal: If they gather troops again, they will once more become a trouble to us, and regret will be too late!
translations.idiomatic: If they rally their forces again, they will be our trouble once more, and it will be too late for regret!

sentences.zh: 戰尚神速，何明旦也！

translations.literal: In warfare speed is prized—why wait until tomorrow!
translations.idiomatic: War favors speed—why wait until dawn!

sentences.zh: 」俶固止之，使還營。

translations.literal: " Chu firmly restrained him and had him return to camp.
translations.idiomatic: " Chu held firm and sent him back to camp.

sentences.zh: 懷恩固請，往而復反，一夕四五起。

translations.literal: Huai'en pressed his request insistently, going and coming back again, four or five times in one night.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en pleaded again and again, going to Chu and returning four or five times that night alone.

sentences.zh: 遲明，諜至，守忠、歸仁與張通儒、田乾真等皆已遁矣。

translations.literal: At dawn scouts arrived: Shouzhong, Guiren, Zhang Tongru, Tian Qianzhen, and the rest had all already fled.
translations.idiomatic: At first light scouts reported that Shouzhong, Guiren, Zhang Tongru, Tian Qianzhen, and the others had already escaped.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，大軍入西京。

translations.literal: On day guimao the great army entered the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the main army entered the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 初，上欲速得京師，與回紇約曰：「克城之日，土地、士庶歸唐，金帛、子女皆歸回紇。

translations.literal: Earlier, because the emperor wished to recover the capital quickly, he had agreed with the Uyghurs: "On the day the city is taken, land and common people shall belong to Tang; gold, silk, and women and children shall all belong to the Uyghurs.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, eager to recover the capital quickly, the emperor had promised the Uyghurs: "When the city falls, the land and people revert to Tang; gold, silk, and captives are yours.

sentences.zh: 」至是，葉護欲如約。

translations.literal: " Now Yabgu wished to act according to the agreement.
translations.idiomatic: " Now Yabgu meant to hold him to that bargain.

sentences.zh: 廣平王俶拜於葉護馬前曰：「今始得西京，若遽俘掠，則東京之人皆為賊固守，不可復取矣，願至東京乃如約。

translations.literal: The Prince of Guangping Li Chu bowed before Yabgu's horse and said: "We have only just taken the Western Capital; if you seize and plunder at once, then the people of the Eastern Capital will all hold firm for the rebels and it cannot be retaken; I beg that we act according to the agreement only when we reach the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Guangping Li Chu bowed before Yabgu's horse and said: "We have only just taken Chang'an. If you loot the city now, the people of Luoyang will stand firm for the rebels and we will never retake it. Grant us your forbearance until Luoyang falls, and then we will honor the agreement in full.

sentences.zh: 」葉護驚躍下馬答拜，跪捧王足，曰：「當為殿下徑往東京。

translations.literal: " Yabgu, startled, leaped down from his horse and returned the bow; kneeling, he held the prince's feet and said: "I shall go straight to the Eastern Capital for Your Highness.
translations.idiomatic: " Startled, Yabgu leapt down and returned the bow. Kneeling, he took the prince's feet in his hands and said: "I shall march straight on Luoyang for Your Highness.

sentences.zh: 」即與僕固懷恩引回紇、西域之兵自城南過，營於滻水之東。

translations.literal: " Immediately, with Pugu Huai'en, he led the Uyghur and Western Region troops through the south of the city and encamped east of the Ba River.
translations.idiomatic: " At once he and Pugu Huai'en led the Uyghur and Western Region troops through the southern quarter and pitched camp east of the Ba River.

sentences.zh: 百姓、軍士、胡虜見俶拜者，皆泣曰：「廣平王真華、夷之主！

translations.literal: Common people, soldiers, and barbarians who saw Chu bow all wept and said: "The Prince of Guangping is truly a lord of both Chinese and barbarians!
translations.idiomatic: Civilians, soldiers, and tribesmen who witnessed Chu's bow wept and said: "The Prince of Guangping is truly a lord for Chinese and barbarian alike!

sentences.zh: 」上聞之，喜曰：「朕不及也！

translations.literal: " When the emperor heard of it, he said with delight: "I cannot match him!
translations.idiomatic: " When the emperor heard this, he said with delight: "He has surpassed me!

sentences.zh: 」俶整眾入城，百姓老幼夾道歡呼悲泣。

translations.literal: " Chu put his troops in order and entered the city; old and young among the common people lined the roads, shouting for joy and weeping.
translations.idiomatic: " Chu formed his troops and entered the city. Old and young lined the streets, shouting for joy through their tears.

sentences.zh: 俶留長安，鎮撫三日，引大軍東出。

translations.literal: Chu remained in Chang'an, pacifying and reassuring for three days, then led the great army eastward.
translations.idiomatic: Chu remained in Chang'an for three days to restore order, then marched east with the main army.

sentences.zh: 以太子少傅虢王巨為西京留守。

translations.literal: He appointed the Prince of Guo Ju, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, as garrison commander of the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: He left Prince of Guo Ju, Grand Tutor to the Heir Apparent, as garrison commander of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，捷書至鳳翔，百寮入賀。

translations.literal: On day jiachen the victory report reached Fengxiang, and the hundred officials entered to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen the victory dispatch reached Fengxiang, and the court officials came in to offer congratulations.

sentences.zh: 上涕泗交頤，即日，遣中使啖庭瑤入蜀奏上皇，命左僕射裴冕入京師，告郊廟及宣慰百姓。

translations.literal: The emperor's tears and mucus mingled on his chin; that same day he dispatched the palace envoy Dan Tingyao into Shu to report to the Retired Emperor, and ordered the Left Vice Director Pei Mian to enter the capital, announce the news at the suburban altars and ancestral temples, and comfort and reassure the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Tears streamed down the emperor's face. That same day he sent the palace envoy Dan Tingyao into Shu to report to the Retired Emperor, and ordered Left Vice Director Pei Mian to enter the capital to announce the victory at the suburban altars and ancestral temples and to comfort the people.

sentences.zh: 上以駿馬召李泌於長安。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a swift horse to summon Li Mi from Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a relay of swift horses to summon Li Mi from Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 既至，上曰：「朕已表請上皇東歸，朕當還東宮復修人子之職。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the emperor said: "I have already memorialized requesting that the Retired Emperor return east; I shall return to the Eastern Palace and resume the duties of a son.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived, the emperor said: "I have already submitted a memorial asking the Retired Emperor to return east. I shall go back to the Eastern Palace and resume my duties as a son.

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「表可追乎？

translations.literal: " Mi said: "Can the memorial still be recalled?
translations.idiomatic: " Mi asked: "Can that memorial still be recalled?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「已遠矣。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "It is already far off.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "It is already far on its way.

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「上皇不來矣。

translations.literal: " Mi said: "The Retired Emperor will not come.
translations.idiomatic: " Mi said: "Then the Retired Emperor will not come.

sentences.zh: 」上驚，問故。

translations.literal: " The emperor was startled and asked the reason.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor started and asked why.

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「理勢自然」。

translations.literal: Mi said: "It is the natural course of reason and circumstance."
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "That is simply how reason and circumstance work."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「為之奈何？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "What is to be done about it?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked: "What can be done?"

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「今請更為群臣賀表，言自馬嵬請留，靈武勸進，及今成功，聖上思戀晨昏，請速還京以就孝養之意，則可矣。

translations.literal: " Mi said: "Now please have the officials submit a new congratulatory memorial, stating that from Mawei you asked him to remain, at Lingwu you were urged to ascend, and now that success is achieved, Your Majesty longs for him morning and evening and asks that he return quickly to the capital to fulfill the intent of filial support—then it will do.
translations.idiomatic: " Mi said: "Have the officials submit a fresh congratulatory memorial. Say that from Mawei you begged him to stay, that at Lingwu the court urged your accession, and that now, with victory won, you long for him day and night and beg him to return quickly to the capital so you may care for him in filial duty. That will suffice."

sentences.zh: 」上即使泌草表。

translations.literal: " The emperor immediately had Mi draft the memorial.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor at once had Mi draft the memorial.

sentences.zh: 上讀之，泣曰：「朕始以至誠願歸萬機。

translations.literal: The emperor read it and wept, saying: "At first I wished with utmost sincerity to return the myriad affairs of state.
translations.idiomatic: Reading it, the emperor wept and said: "At first I meant in all sincerity to return the reins of government."

sentences.zh: 今聞先生之言，乃寤其失。

translations.literal: Now, hearing the Master's words, I have awakened to my error.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing your words now, I see my mistake."

sentences.zh: 」立命中使奉表入蜀，因就泌飲酒，同榻而寢。

translations.literal: " He immediately ordered a palace envoy to carry the memorial into Shu; then he drank with Mi and they slept on the same couch.
translations.idiomatic: " He immediately ordered a palace envoy to carry the memorial into Shu, then drank with Mi and they slept on the same couch.

sentences.zh: 而李輔國請取契鑰付泌，泌請使輔國掌之；

translations.literal: Meanwhile Li Fuguo asked to take the seals and keys and hand them to Mi; Mi asked that Fuguo keep charge of them;
translations.idiomatic: Li Fuguo asked to hand the seals and keys to Mi; Mi asked instead that Fuguo keep charge of them;

sentences.zh: 上許之。

translations.literal: the emperor granted it.
translations.idiomatic: and the emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「臣今報德足矣，復為閒人，何樂如之！

translations.literal: Mi said: "Your servant has now repaid your grace fully; to become a free man again—what joy could equal it!
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "I have repaid your grace. To become a free man again—what could bring greater joy!"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕與先生累年同憂患，今方相同娛樂，奈何遽欲去乎！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I and the Master have shared years of hardship together; we have only now begun to share pleasure—why do you so hastily wish to leave!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "You and I have shared years of hardship. We have only just begun to enjoy peace together—why are you in such haste to go!"

sentences.zh: 」泌曰：「臣有五不可留，願陛下聽臣去，免臣於死。

translations.literal: " Mi said: "Your servant has five reasons why he cannot remain; I beg Your Majesty to let me go and spare me from death.
translations.idiomatic: " Mi said: "I have five reasons why I cannot stay. Grant me leave, Majesty, and spare my life."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「何謂也？

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "What do you mean?
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor asked: "What do you mean?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「臣遇陛下太早，陛下任臣太重，寵臣太深，臣功太高，跡太奇，此其所以不可留也。

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your servant met Your Majesty too early; Your Majesty entrusted me too heavily, favored me too deeply, my achievements are too high, and my course too singular—these are the reasons why I cannot remain.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "I met you too early; you entrusted me with too much, favored me too deeply, my achievements are too great, and my conduct too singular. That is why I cannot stay."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「且眠矣，異日議之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Sleep for now; we shall discuss it another day.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "Sleep now. We will discuss it another day."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下今就臣榻臥，猶不得請，況異日香案之前乎！

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your Majesty now lies on my couch, yet I still cannot obtain my request—how much less on some future day before the incense table!
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "Even now, as you lie on my couch, I cannot obtain my request—how much less on some future day before the throne!"

sentences.zh: 陛下不聽臣去，是殺臣也。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty will not hear my request to go, you are killing me.
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty will not let me go, you are killing me.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「不意卿疑朕如此，豈有如朕而辦殺卿邪！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I did not expect you to suspect me so—would there be one like me who could bear to kill you!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "I never thought you suspected me so. Would I, of all men, bear to kill you!"

sentences.zh: 是直以朕為句踐也！

translations.literal: You are simply taking me for Goujian!
translations.idiomatic: You take me for Goujian himself!"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下不辦殺臣，故臣求歸；

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your Majesty cannot yet bear to kill me, and therefore I ask to withdraw;
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "Your Majesty cannot yet bring yourself to kill me, and that is why I ask to leave now;

sentences.zh: 若其既辦，臣安得復言！

translations.literal: once you can bear to do so, how could I speak again!
translations.idiomatic: once you can, how could I still speak!"

sentences.zh: 且殺臣者，非陛下也，乃『五不可』也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the one who would kill me is not Your Majesty but the 'five reasons why I cannot remain.'
translations.idiomatic: Besides, it is not Your Majesty who would kill me, but the 'five reasons why I cannot stay.'"

sentences.zh: 陛下向日待臣如此，臣於事猶有不敢言者，況天下既安，臣敢言乎！

translations.literal: When Your Majesty treated me as you did in the past, there were still matters on which I dared not speak—how much less now that the realm is at peace: would I dare speak!
translations.idiomatic: Even when you favored me as you did, there were things I dared not say. Now that the realm is at peace, how could I dare speak!"

sentences.zh: 上良久曰：「卿以朕不從卿北伐之謀乎！

translations.literal: After a long silence the emperor said: "Do you think it is because I did not follow your plan for a northern campaign!
translations.idiomatic: After a long silence the emperor said: "Do you think this is because I refused your plan for a northern campaign!"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「非也，所不敢言者，乃建寧耳。

translations.literal: " He replied: "No; what I dared not speak of is Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "No. What I dared not speak of is the Prince of Jianning."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「建寧，朕之愛子，性英果，艱難時有功，朕豈不知之！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Jianning is my beloved son—by nature bold and resolute, with merit in hard times; how could I not know it!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "Jianning was my beloved son—bold, resolute, and meritorious in our darkest days. Do you think I did not know that!"

sentences.zh: 但因此為小人所教，欲害其兄，圖繼嗣，朕以社稷大計，不得已而除之。

translations.literal: But because of this he was taught by petty men, wished to harm his elder brother, and plotted for the succession; for the great plan of the altars of state I had no choice but to remove him.
translations.idiomatic: But petty men turned him against his elder brother and taught him to plot for the succession. For the sake of the realm I had no choice but to remove him."

sentences.zh: 卿不細知其故邪？

translations.literal: Do you not know the details of the reason?
translations.idiomatic: Do you not know the full story?"

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「若有此心，廣平當怨之。

translations.literal: " He replied: "If he had such a heart, Guangping ought to resent him.
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "If that were true, Guangping would resent him."

sentences.zh: 廣平每與臣言其冤，輒流涕嗚咽。

translations.literal: Whenever Guangping speaks to me of his injustice, he always weeps and sobs.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Guangping speaks to me of his brother's injustice, he weeps until he can barely speak.

sentences.zh: 臣今必辭陛下去，始敢言之耳。

translations.literal: Only now that I must take leave of Your Majesty do I dare speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Only because I am leaving your service do I dare say this now."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「渠嘗夜捫廣平，意欲加害。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "He once felt Guangping in the night, intending to do him harm.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "He once felt for Guangping in the night, meaning to kill him."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「此皆出讒人之口，豈有建寧之孝友聰明，肯為此乎！

translations.literal: " He replied: "All this comes from the mouths of slanderers—how could Jianning, filial, friendly, and intelligent, have been willing to do such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "That is all slander. How could Jianning, so filial, loyal, and bright, have done such a thing!"

sentences.zh: 且陛下昔欲用建寧為元帥，臣請用廣平。

translations.literal: Moreover, when Your Majesty once wished to make Jianning commander-in-chief, I asked that Guangping be used instead.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, when Your Majesty once meant to make Jianning supreme commander, I urged Guangping instead."

sentences.zh: 建寧若有此心，當深憾於臣；

translations.literal: If Jianning had such a heart, he ought to have deeply resented me;
translations.idiomatic: If Jianning harbored such a heart, he would have deeply resented me;

sentences.zh: 而以臣為忠，益相親善，陛下以此可察其心矣。

translations.literal: yet he regarded me as loyal and grew ever closer and kinder—Your Majesty may judge his heart by this.
translations.idiomatic: yet he treated me as loyal and grew ever closer to me. By that, Majesty, you may judge his heart."

sentences.zh: 」上乃泣下曰：「先生言是也。

translations.literal: " The emperor then wept and said: "The Master speaks rightly.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor wept and said: "You are right, Master."

sentences.zh: 既往不咎，朕不欲聞之。

translations.literal: What is past is not to be blamed; I do not wish to hear of it again.
translations.idiomatic: What is past is past. I do not wish to hear of it again."

sentences.zh: 泌曰：「臣所以言之者，非咎既往，乃欲陛下慎將來耳。

translations.literal: Mi said: "The reason your servant spoke of it is not to blame what is past, but to wish that Your Majesty be cautious about what is to come.
translations.idiomatic: Mi said: "I spoke of this not to blame the past, but to urge Your Majesty to be careful in the days ahead.

sentences.zh: 昔天後有四子，長曰太子弘，天後方圖稱制，惡其聰明，鴆殺之，立次子雍王賢。

translations.literal: In the past the Empress Tianhou had four sons; the eldest was the Heir Apparent Hong. The Empress Tianhou was then plotting to seize power herself and hated his intelligence; she poisoned him and established the second son, the Prince of Yong Xian.
translations.idiomatic: Long ago Empress Wu had four sons. The eldest, Heir Apparent Hong, was so bright that she, plotting to rule in her own name, poisoned him and set up her second son, Prince of Yong Xian, instead.

sentences.zh: 賢內憂懼，作《黃台瓜辭》，冀以感悟天後。

translations.literal: Xian, inwardly anxious and fearful, composed the "Melon Beneath the Yellow Terrace" poem, hoping thereby to move the Empress Tianhou to feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Xian, sick with fear, wrote the "Melons Beneath the Yellow Terrace" poem, hoping to move the empress's heart.

sentences.zh: 天後不聽，賢卒死於黔中。

translations.literal: The Empress Tianhou would not listen, and Xian ultimately died in Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: The empress would not listen, and Xian died in exile at Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：『種瓜黃台下，瓜熟子離離。

translations.literal: The poem says: 'Melons planted beneath the Yellow Terrace; when ripe, the fruits hang thick.
translations.idiomatic: The poem runs: "Melons planted beneath the Yellow Terrace; when ripe, the fruits hang thick.

sentences.zh: 一摘使瓜好，再摘使瓜稀，三摘猶為可，四摘抱蔓歸！

translations.literal: One plucking makes the melons better; a second plucking makes them sparse; a third plucking is still bearable; a fourth plucking leaves only the vines to carry home!'
translations.idiomatic: One picking leaves good melons; a second leaves few; a third is still tolerable; a fourth leaves only the vines to carry home!"

sentences.zh: 』今陛下已一摘矣，慎無再摘！

translations.literal: ' Now Your Majesty has already plucked once—take care not to pluck again!
translations.idiomatic: " Your Majesty has already plucked once. Take care not to pluck again!"

sentences.zh: 」上愕然曰：「安有是哉！

translations.literal: " The emperor said in astonishment: "How could there be such a thing!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said in astonishment: "Surely not!"

sentences.zh: 」卿錄是辭，朕當書紳。

translations.literal: " You shall copy out this poem; I shall write it on my girdle.
translations.idiomatic: " Copy out that poem. I shall write it on my sash."

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「陛下但識之於心，何必形於外也！

translations.literal: " He replied: "Your Majesty need only keep it in your heart—why must it take outward form!
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "Keep it in your heart, Majesty. There is no need to wear it outwardly."

sentences.zh: 」是時廣平王有大功，良娣忌之，潛構流言，故泌言及之。

translations.literal: " At this time the Prince of Guangping had great merit; the Lady of Excellence envied him and secretly spread slanderous talk—therefore Mi spoke of it.
translations.idiomatic: " The Prince of Guangping had just won great merit, and the Lady of Excellence, jealous of him, was spreading secret slanders—hence Mi's warning.

sentences.zh: 泌復固請歸山，上曰：「俟將發此議之。

translations.literal: Mi again pressed his request to return to the mountains; the emperor said: "Wait until we are about to set out, and we shall discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: Mi again begged to return to the mountains. The emperor said: "Wait until we are about to march, and we will discuss it then.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀引蕃、漢兵追賊至潼關，斬首五千級，克華陰、弘農二郡。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi led barbarian and Han troops in pursuit of the rebels to Tong Pass, cut off five thousand heads, and captured the two commanderies of Huayin and Hongnong.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi pursued the rebels to Tong Pass with allied and Han troops, took five thousand heads, and recovered Huayin and Hongnong.

sentences.zh: 關東獻俘百餘人，敕皆斬之；

translations.literal: The east of the passes presented more than a hundred captives; an edict ordered that all be beheaded;
translations.idiomatic: More than a hundred captives from east of the passes were presented; an edict ordered them all beheaded;

sentences.zh: 監察御史李勉言於上曰：「今元惡未除，為賊所污者半天下，聞陛下龍興，鹹思洗心以承聖化，今悉誅之，是驅之使從賊也。

translations.literal: the Investigating Censor Li Mian said to the emperor: "Now the chief villain is not yet removed; half the realm has been stained by the rebels. Hearing that Your Majesty has risen like a dragon, all wish to wash their hearts and receive your sage transformation. If you now execute them all, you will drive them to follow the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: but Investigating Censor Li Mian told the emperor: "The chief villain is not yet destroyed, and half the realm has been tainted by the rebels. When they hear that Your Majesty has risen, they all wish to cleanse their hearts and submit to your rule. Execute them all now, and you will drive them back to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 」上遽使赦之。

translations.literal: " The emperor immediately had them pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor at once ordered them pardoned.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，丁未，啖庭瑤至蜀。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, day dingwei: Dan Tingyao reached Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on dingwei, Dan Tingyao reached Shu.

sentences.zh: 壬子，興平軍奏：破賊於武關，克上洛郡。

translations.literal: On day renzi the Xingping Army reported: they defeated the rebels at Wu Pass and captured Shangluo commandery.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi the Xingping Army reported a victory at Wu Pass and the capture of Shangluo commandery.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃陷西平。

translations.literal: The Tibetans captured Xiping.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans took Xiping.

sentences.zh: 尹子奇久圍睢陽，城中食盡，議棄城東走，張巡、許遠謀，以為：「睢陽，江、淮之保障，若棄之去，賊必乘勝長驅，是無江、淮也。

translations.literal: Yin Ziqi had long besieged Suiyang; food in the city was exhausted, and there was discussion of abandoning the city and fleeing east. Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan deliberated and held: "Suiyang is the bulwark of the Yangzi and Huai regions. If we abandon it and leave, the rebels will surely press their victory in a long drive, and there will be no Yangzi or Huai.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ziqi had long besieged Suiyang. When food ran out, some urged abandoning the city and fleeing east. Zhang Xun and Xu Yuan argued: "Suiyang is the shield of the Yangzi and Huai valleys. If we leave it, the rebels will sweep south unchecked, and the lower Yangzi will be lost.

sentences.zh: 且我眾饑羸，走必不達。

translations.literal: Moreover, our forces are hungry and weak; if we flee we surely cannot get far.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, our men are starving and weak; if we flee, we will not get far.

sentences.zh: 古者戰國諸侯，尚相救恤，況密邇群帥乎！

translations.literal: In antiquity even the feudal lords of the Warring States still aided one another—how much more so nearby commanders!
translations.idiomatic: Even the feudal lords of the Warring States aided one another—how much more should nearby commanders do so!

sentences.zh: 不如堅守以待之。

translations.literal: It is better to hold firm and wait.
translations.idiomatic: Better to hold the city and wait for relief.

sentences.zh: 」茶紙既盡，遂食馬；

translations.literal: " When tea and paper were exhausted, they then ate the horses;
translations.idiomatic: " When tea and paper were gone, they ate the horses;

sentences.zh: 馬盡，羅雀掘鼠；

translations.literal: when the horses were gone, they netted sparrows and dug out rats;
translations.idiomatic: when the horses were gone, they netted sparrows and dug out rats;

sentences.zh: 雀鼠又盡，巡出愛妾，殺以食士，遠亦殺其奴；

translations.literal: when sparrows and rats too were gone, Xun gave up his beloved concubine and killed her to feed the soldiers; Yuan also killed his slave;
translations.idiomatic: when even sparrows and rats were gone, Xun killed his beloved concubine to feed the troops, and Yuan killed his slave;

sentences.zh: 然後括城中婦人食之；

translations.literal: then they gathered the women of the city to be eaten;
translations.idiomatic: then they turned to the women of the city;

sentences.zh: 既盡，繼以男子老弱。

translations.literal: when these were exhausted, they followed with old and weak men.
translations.idiomatic: when they were gone, the old and weak men followed.

sentences.zh: 人知必死，莫有叛者，所餘才四百人。

translations.literal: Knowing they must die, none rebelled; only four hundred remained.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing death was certain, none deserted; only four hundred were left.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，賊登城，將士病，不能戰。

translations.literal: On day guichou the rebels climbed the walls; the officers and soldiers were ill and could not fight.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou the rebels scaled the walls. The garrison was sick and could not fight.

sentences.zh: 巡西向再拜曰：「臣力竭矣，不能全城，生既無以報陛下，死當為厲鬼以殺賊！

translations.literal: Xun bowed twice toward the west and said: "Your servant's strength is exhausted; I cannot preserve the whole city. In life I had no means to repay Your Majesty; in death I shall become a vengeful ghost to slay the rebels!
translations.idiomatic: Xun bowed twice toward the west and said: "My strength is spent and I cannot save the city. Living, I could not repay Your Majesty; dead, I shall be a vengeful ghost and kill rebels!"

sentences.zh: 」城遂陷，巡、遠俱被執。

translations.literal: " The city then fell; Xun and Yuan were both captured.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell. Xun and Yuan were both taken.

sentences.zh: 尹子奇問巡曰：「聞君每戰眥裂齒碎，何也？

translations.literal: Yin Ziqi asked Xun: "I hear that in every battle your eyes split and your teeth shatter—why?
translations.idiomatic: Yin Ziqi asked Xun: "They say that in every battle your eyes split and your teeth shatter. Why?"

sentences.zh: 」巡曰：「吾志吞逆賊，但力不能耳！

translations.literal: " Xun said: "My will is to swallow the rebel bandits, but my strength cannot do it!
translations.idiomatic: " Xun said: "My will is to destroy the rebels, but my strength falls short!"

sentences.zh: 」子奇以刀抉其口視之，所餘才三四。

translations.literal: " Ziqi pried open his mouth with a knife and looked; only three or four teeth remained.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqi pried open his mouth with a knife: only three or four teeth were left.

sentences.zh: 子奇義其所為，欲活之。

translations.literal: Ziqi admired his conduct and wished to spare his life.
translations.idiomatic: Ziqi admired his conduct and wished to spare him.

sentences.zh: 其徒曰：「彼守節者也，終不為吾用。

translations.literal: His followers said: "He is one who holds to integrity; in the end he will not serve us.
translations.idiomatic: His followers said: "He is a man of integrity and will never serve us.

sentences.zh: 且得士心，存之，將為後患。

translations.literal: Moreover, if we win the soldiers' hearts by sparing him, keeping him alive will become a trouble for later.
translations.idiomatic: Besides, if we win the soldiers' hearts by sparing him, he will become a danger later."

sentences.zh: 」乃並南霽雲、雷萬春等三十六人皆斬之。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they beheaded Nan Jiyun, Lei Wanchun, and thirty-six others together.
translations.idiomatic: They then beheaded Nan Jiyun, Lei Wanchun, and thirty-six others together.

sentences.zh: 巡且死，顏色不亂，揚揚如常。

translations.literal: As Xun was about to die, his countenance was not disturbed; he was buoyant as usual.
translations.idiomatic: As Xun faced death, his face did not change; he bore himself as calmly as ever.

sentences.zh: 生致許遠於洛陽。

translations.literal: Xu Yuan was taken alive to Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan was taken alive to Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 巡初守睢陽時，卒僅萬人，城中居人亦且數萬，巡一見問姓名，其後無不識者。

translations.literal: When Xun first defended Suiyang, his soldiers numbered only ten thousand, and the residents in the city were also nearly tens of thousands; after one meeting in which he asked their names, thereafter there was none he did not recognize.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun first held Suiyang, he had barely ten thousand soldiers and tens of thousands of civilians. After one meeting in which he asked each man's name, he never forgot a face.

sentences.zh: 前後大小戰凡四百餘，殺賊卒十二萬人。

translations.literal: Before and after, great and small battles totaled more than four hundred; rebel soldiers killed numbered one hundred twenty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In more than four hundred engagements, great and small, they killed a hundred and twenty thousand rebels.

sentences.zh: 巡行兵不依古法教戰陳，令本將各以其意教之。

translations.literal: Xun in moving troops did not teach battle formations according to ancient methods; he ordered each original commander to teach according to his own understanding.
translations.idiomatic: Xun did not drill his men in classical battle formations. He let each commander train his own men as he saw fit.

sentences.zh: 人或問其故，巡曰：「今與胡虜戰，雲合鳥散，變態不恆。

translations.literal: When someone asked the reason, Xun said: "Now we fight the barbarians; they gather like clouds and scatter like birds, their transformations inconstant.
translations.idiomatic: When asked why, Xun said: "We fight barbarians who gather like clouds and scatter like birds, shifting without pattern.

sentences.zh: 數步之間，勢有同異。

translations.literal: Within a few paces the situation may differ.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few paces the situation can change.

sentences.zh: 臨機應猝，在於呼吸之間，而動詢大將，事不相及，非知兵之變者也。

translations.literal: Adapting on the spot to sudden crises lies in the space between breaths; yet to move and consult a great general—the affair would not keep pace. That is not to understand the changes of warfare.
translations.idiomatic: To respond on the instant takes but a breath, yet to run every move past a senior commander is too slow. That is not how war works.

sentences.zh: 故吾使兵識將意，將識士情，投之而往，如手之使指。

translations.literal: Therefore I make the soldiers know the commanders' intent and the commanders know the soldiers' temper; cast them forward and they go, like the hand moving the fingers.
translations.idiomatic: So I make soldiers know their commanders' intent and commanders know their men. Send them forward and they go like fingers on a hand.

sentences.zh: 兵將相習，人自為戰，不亦可乎！

translations.literal: Soldiers and commanders accustomed to one another, each man fighting on his own—is that not acceptable!
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men know one another, and each fights on his own initiative—is that not enough!"

sentences.zh: 」自興兵，器械、甲仗皆取之於敵，未嘗自修。

translations.literal: " From the time he raised troops, weapons and armor were all taken from the enemy; he never repaired his own.
translations.idiomatic: From the day he took the field, weapons and armor all came from the enemy; he never maintained his own stores.

sentences.zh: 每戰，將士或退散，巡立於戰所，謂將士曰：「我不離此，汝為我還決之。

translations.literal: In every battle, when officers and soldiers sometimes scattered in retreat, Xun would stand at the place of fighting and say to the officers and soldiers: "I will not leave this spot; fight it out for me and return.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever his men broke, Xun would stand his ground and call: "I am not leaving this spot. Go back and settle it for me."

sentences.zh: 」將士莫敢不還死戰，卒破敵。

translations.literal: " The officers and soldiers dared not fail to return and fight to the death, and in the end broke the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: None dared do otherwise; they turned back and fought to the death, and in the end broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 又推誠待人，無所疑隱；

translations.literal: He also treated men with sincere trust, without suspicion or concealment;
translations.idiomatic: He also treated men with open sincerity, without suspicion;

sentences.zh: 臨敵應變，出奇無窮；

translations.literal: facing the enemy he adapted and changed, his stratagems inexhaustible;
translations.idiomatic: facing the enemy he adapted endlessly, his stratagems inexhaustible;

sentences.zh: 號令明，賞罰信，與眾共甘苦寒暑，故下爭致死力。

translations.literal: his orders were clear, rewards and punishments trustworthy, and he shared with the multitude bitter cold and heat—therefore those below strove to give their utmost strength.
translations.idiomatic: his orders were clear, rewards and punishments sure, and he shared heat and cold with his men—so they fought to the death for him.

sentences.zh: 張鎬聞睢陽圍急，倍道亟進，檄浙東、浙西、淮南、北海諸節度及譙郡太守閭丘曉，使共救之。

translations.literal: Zhang Gao, hearing that the siege of Suiyang was urgent, advanced at double speed by forced marches, and issued summons to the military commissioners of Zhedong, Zhexi, Huainan, and Beihai and to Yanqiu Xiao, prefect of Qiao commandery, to join in rescuing it.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Suiyang was in desperate straits, Zhang Gao forced the march and summoned the commissioners of Zhedong, Zhexi, Huainan, and Beihai, and Qiao commandery prefect Yanqiu Xiao, to relieve the city.

sentences.zh: 曉素傲很，不受鎬命。

translations.literal: Xiao was by nature arrogant and obstinate and would not accept Gao's orders.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao was proud and obstinate and refused Gao's orders.

sentences.zh: 比鎬至，睢陽城已陷三日。

translations.literal: By the time Gao arrived, Suiyang had already fallen three days before.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Gao arrived, Suiyang had fallen three days earlier.

sentences.zh: 鎬召曉，杖殺之。

translations.literal: Gao summoned Xiao and had him beaten to death with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: Gao summoned Xiao and had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 張通儒等收餘眾走保陝，安慶緒悉發洛陽兵，使其御史大夫嚴莊將之，就通儒以拒官軍，並舊兵步騎猶十五萬。

translations.literal: Zhang Tongru and the others gathered the remaining troops and fled to hold Shan; An Qingxu sent out all the Luoyang troops, having his Censor-in-Chief Yan Zhuang lead them to join Tongru in resisting the government army; together with the old troops, infantry and cavalry still numbered one hundred fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Tongru and the others rallied the survivors and fell back on Shan. An Qingxu sent out every soldier in Luoyang under Censor-in-Chief Yan Zhuang to join Tongru against the imperial army. Old and new troops together still numbered a hundred and fifty thousand.

sentences.zh: 己未，廣平王俶至曲沃。

translations.literal: On day jiwei the Prince of Guangping Li Chu reached Quwo.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei Prince of Guangping Li Chu reached Quwo.

sentences.zh: 回紇葉護使其將軍鼻施吐撥裴羅等引軍旁南山搜伏，因駐軍嶺北。

translations.literal: The Uyghur Yabgu ordered his generals Bishi Tubo Peiluo and others to lead troops along the southern mountains searching out ambushes, and encamped north of the ridge.
translations.idiomatic: Yabgu sent Generals Bishi Tubo Peiluo and others to sweep the southern hills for ambushes and camped north of the ridge.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀等與賊遇於新店，賊依山而陳。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi and the others encountered the rebels at Xindian; the rebels formed battle lines relying on the hills.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi met the rebels at Xindian, where they drew up on the hills.

sentences.zh: 子儀等初與之戰，不利，賊逐之下山。

translations.literal: Ziyi and the others at first fought them with unfavorable results; the rebels pursued them down the hill.
translations.idiomatic: At first the imperial forces fought poorly and the rebels drove them down the slope.

sentences.zh: 回紇自南山襲其背，於黃埃中發十餘矢。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs from the southern mountains struck their rear, loosing more than ten arrows in the yellow dust.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs struck from the southern hills into the rebels' rear, loosing a volley through the yellow dust.

sentences.zh: 賊驚顧曰：「回紇至矣！

translations.literal: The rebels looked back in alarm and cried: "The Uyghurs have come!
translations.idiomatic: The rebels looked back in alarm and cried: "The Uyghurs are here!"

sentences.zh: 」遂潰。

translations.literal: " Thereupon they broke.
translations.idiomatic: They broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 官軍與回紇夾擊之，賊大敗，殭屍蔽野。

translations.literal: The government army and the Uyghurs struck them from both sides; the rebels were greatly defeated, and corpses covered the fields.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial army and the Uyghurs struck them from both sides. The rebels were routed, and the fields were heaped with corpses.

sentences.zh: 嚴莊、張通儒等棄陝東走，廣平王俶、郭子儀入陝城，僕固懷恩等分道追之。

translations.literal: Yan Zhuang, Zhang Tongru, and the others abandoned Shan and fled east; the Prince of Guangping Li Chu and Guo Ziyi entered Shan city; Pugu Huai'en and others pursued along separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhuang and Zhang Tongru abandoned Shan and fled east. Prince of Guangping Li Chu and Guo Ziyi entered the city, while Pugu Huai'en and others pursued along separate routes.

sentences.zh: 嚴莊先入洛陽告安慶緒。

translations.literal: Yan Zhuang entered Luoyang first to inform An Qingxu.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhuang reached Luoyang first and warned An Qingxu.

sentences.zh: 庚申夜，慶緒帥其黨自苑門出，走河北；

translations.literal: On the night of day gengshen, Qingxu led his faction out through the Garden Gate and fled to Hebei;
translations.idiomatic: On the night of gengshen, Qingxu led his followers out through the Garden Gate and fled to Hebei;

sentences.zh: 殺所獲唐將哥舒翰、程千里等三十餘人而去。

translations.literal: he killed the Tang generals they had captured—Geshu Han, Cheng Qianli, and more than thirty others—and departed.
translations.idiomatic: killing the captured Tang generals Geshu Han, Cheng Qianli, and more than thirty others before he left.

sentences.zh: 許遠死於偃師。

translations.literal: Xu Yuan died at Yanshi.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Yuan was killed at Yanshi.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，廣平王俶入東京。

translations.literal: On day renxu the Prince of Guangping Li Chu entered the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Prince of Guangping Li Chu entered the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 回紇意猶未厭，俶患之。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs' desires were still unsatisfied; Chu was troubled by it.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs were still not satisfied, and Chu was troubled.

sentences.zh: 父老請率羅錦萬匹以賂回紇，回紇乃止。

translations.literal: The elders of the district asked to lead ten thousand bolts of gauze and brocade to bribe the Uyghurs, and the Uyghurs then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The elders offered ten thousand bolts of silk and brocade to appease the Uyghurs, and they desisted.

sentences.zh: 成都使還，上皇誥曰：「當與我劍南一道自奉，不復來矣。

translations.literal: The envoy from Chengdu returned; the Retired Emperor's proclamation said: "I shall support myself with the Jiannan circuit alone and will not come back.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy from Chengdu returned, the Retired Emperor's proclamation said: "I shall keep myself on the Jiannan circuit alone and will not return.

sentences.zh: 」上憂懼，不知所為。

translations.literal: " The emperor was anxious and fearful, not knowing what to do.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was stricken with fear and did not know what to do.

sentences.zh: 數日後，使者至，言：「上皇初得上請歸東宮表，彷徨不能食，欲不歸；

translations.literal: Several days later the messenger arrived and said: "When the Retired Emperor first received Your Majesty's memorial requesting return to the Eastern Palace, he was irresolute and could not eat, wishing not to return;
translations.idiomatic: Several days later another messenger arrived and said: "When the Retired Emperor first received Your Majesty's memorial asking him to return to the Eastern Palace, he was so troubled he could not eat and meant not to come back;

sentences.zh: 及群臣表至，乃大喜，命食作樂，下誥定行日。

translations.literal: when the memorial from the officials arrived, he was then greatly pleased, ordered food and music, and issued a proclamation fixing the day of departure.
translations.idiomatic: but when the officials' memorial arrived, he was overjoyed, ordered a feast and music, and set a date for his departure."

sentences.zh: 」上召李泌告之曰：「皆卿力也！

translations.literal: " The emperor summoned Li Mi and told him: "It is all your doing!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor summoned Li Mi and said: "This is all your work!"

sentences.zh: 」泌求歸山不已，上固留之，不能得，乃聽歸衡山。

translations.literal: " Mi repeatedly asked to return to the mountains; the emperor firmly detained him but could not keep him, and therefore permitted him to return to Heng Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Mi again begged to return to the mountains. The emperor tried to keep him but could not, and at last let him go back to Mount Heng.

sentences.zh: 敕郡縣為之築室於山中，給三品料。

translations.literal: He ordered the commanderies and districts to build him a dwelling in the mountains and supply third-rank provisions.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the local officials to build him a house on the mountain and supply him with third-rank rations.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，上發鳳翔，遣太子太師韋見素入蜀，奉迎上皇。

translations.literal: On day guihai the emperor set out from Fengxiang and dispatched the Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent Wei Jiansu into Shu to welcome the Retired Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai the emperor left Fengxiang and sent Grand Preceptor to the Heir Apparent Wei Jiansu into Shu to welcome the Retired Emperor.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，郭子儀遣左兵馬使張用濟、右武鋒使渾釋之將兵取河陽及河內；

translations.literal: On day yichou Guo Ziyi dispatched the Left Army-and-Horse Commissioner Zhang Yongji and the Right Martial Vanguard Commissioner Hun Shizhi to lead troops and take Heyang and Henei;
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Guo Ziyi sent Left Army-and-Horse Commissioner Zhang Yongji and Right Martial Vanguard Commissioner Hun Shizhi to take Heyang and Henei;

sentences.zh: 嚴莊來降。

translations.literal: Yan Zhuang came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhuang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 陳留人殺尹子奇，舉郡降。

translations.literal: The people of Chenliu killed Yin Ziqi and surrendered the whole commandery.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chenliu killed Yin Ziqi and surrendered the commandery.

sentences.zh: 田承嗣圍來瑱於穎川，亦遣使來降；

translations.literal: Tian Chengsi was besieging Lai Tian at Yingchuan and also sent an envoy to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Tian Chengsi, besieging Lai Tian at Yingchuan, also sent envoys to surrender;

sentences.zh: 郭子儀應之緩，承嗣復叛，與武令珣皆走河北。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi responded too slowly; Chengsi rebelled again and, with Wu Lingxun, both fled to Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: but Guo Ziyi answered too slowly. Chengsi rebelled again and fled to Hebei with Wu Lingxun.

sentences.zh: 制以瑱為淮南節度使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Lai Tian as military commissioner of Huainan.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Lai Tian military commissioner of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，上至望賢宮，得東京捷奏。

translations.literal: On day bingyin the emperor reached Wangxian Palace and received the victory report from the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin the emperor reached Wangxian Palace and received the victory dispatch from Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，上入西京。

translations.literal: On day dingmao the emperor entered the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the emperor entered the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 百姓出國門奉迎，二十里不絕，舞躍呼萬歲，有泣者。

translations.literal: The common people came out beyond the city gate to welcome him, unbroken for twenty li, dancing and leaping and crying "Long live the emperor!"—some weeping.
translations.idiomatic: The people came out beyond the city gate to welcome him for twenty li without a break, dancing and shouting "Long live the emperor!"—many weeping.

sentences.zh: 上入居大明宮。

translations.literal: The emperor entered and took up residence in the Daming Palace.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took up residence in the Daming Palace.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞崔器令百官受賊官爵者皆脫巾徒跣立於含元殿前，搏膺頓首請罪，環之以兵，使百官臨視之。

translations.literal: The Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi ordered all officials who had received offices and ranks from the rebels to remove their caps and stand barefoot before the Hanyuan Hall, beating their breasts and knocking their heads to beg forgiveness, ringed about with soldiers so that the hundred officials might look on.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi ordered every official who had accepted rank from the rebels to remove his cap and stand barefoot before Hanyuan Hall, beating his breast and knocking his head to beg forgiveness, ringed with soldiers while the court looked on.

sentences.zh: 太廟為賊所焚，上素服向廟哭三日。

translations.literal: The Imperial Ancestral Temple had been burned by the rebels; the emperor in plain white garments faced the temple and wept for three days.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Ancestral Temple had been burned by the rebels; the emperor wore plain white and mourned before it for three days.

sentences.zh: 是日，上皇發蜀郡。

translations.literal: That same day the Retired Emperor set out from Shu commandery.
translations.idiomatic: That same day the Retired Emperor left Shu.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒走保鄴郡，改鄴郡為安成府，改元天成；

translations.literal: An Qingxu fled to hold Ye commandery, changed Ye commandery to Ancheng Prefecture, and changed the era name to Tiancheng;
translations.idiomatic: An Qingxu fled to Ye, renamed it Ancheng Prefecture, and proclaimed the era name Tiancheng;

sentences.zh: 從騎不過三百，步卒不過千人，諸將阿史那承慶等散投常山、趙郡、范陽。

translations.literal: his mounted followers did not exceed three hundred, his foot soldiers not a thousand; the generals Ashina Chengqing and others scattered to throw themselves on Changshan, Zhaojun, and Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: with fewer than three hundred horsemen and a thousand foot soldiers. Generals such as Ashina Chengqing scattered to Changshan, Zhaojun, and Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 旬日間，蔡希德自上黨，田承嗣自穎川，武令珣自南陽，各帥所部兵歸之。

translations.literal: Within a span of ten days, Cai Xide from Shangdang, Tian Chengsi from Yingchuan, and Wu Lingxun from Nanyang each led the troops under their command to rejoin him.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days, Cai Xide marched down from Shangdang, Tian Chengsi from Yingchuan, and Wu Lingxun from Nanyang, each bringing his division back to his side.

sentences.zh: 又召募河北諸郡人，眾至六萬，軍聲復振。

translations.literal: He also recruited men from the various commanderies north of the Yellow River; the host reached sixty thousand, and the army's prestige revived.
translations.idiomatic: He also raised recruits from the Hebei commanderies until his force numbered sixty thousand, and the army's morale surged anew.

sentences.zh: 廣平王俶之入東京也，百官受安祿山父子官者陳希烈等三百餘人，皆素服悲泣請罪。

translations.literal: When Li Chu, Prince of Guangping, entered the Eastern Capital, more than three hundred officials including Chen Xilie who had accepted offices from An Lushan and his son all wore plain dress, wept in grief, and begged forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Chu, Prince of Guangping, entered the Eastern Capital, more than three hundred officials who had taken office under An Lushan and his son—including Chen Xilie—appeared in undyed mourning dress, weeping as they pleaded for pardon.

sentences.zh: 俶以上旨釋之，尋勒赴西京。

translations.literal: Li Chu released them by the supreme command; soon they were compelled to proceed to the Western Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chu released them by imperial order and soon had them escorted on to the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 己巳，崔器令詣朝堂請罪，如西京百官之儀，然後收系大理、京兆獄。

translations.literal: On day jisi, Cui Qi ordered them to go to the imperial court to beg forgiveness in the same ceremony as the Western Capital officials, then detained them in the prisons of the Court of Judicial Review and the capital prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi day, Cui Qi required them to present themselves at court and perform the same rite of confession as the officials in the Western Capital, after which they were confined in the prisons of the Court of Judicial Review and the metropolitan prefecture.

sentences.zh: 其府縣所由、祗承人等受賊驅使追捕者，皆收系之。

translations.literal: Those subordinate clerks and attendants in the prefectures and counties who had been driven by the rebels to pursue people were all also detained.
translations.idiomatic: Local clerks and runners who had been forced by the rebels to hunt down fugitives were imprisoned as well.

sentences.zh: 初，汲郡甄濟，有操行，隱居青巖山，安祿山為採訪使，奏掌書記。

translations.literal: Initially, Zhen Ji of Jijun had integrity of conduct and lived in seclusion on Mount Qingyan; when An Lushan was regional commissioner, he memorialized that Ji should serve as secretary.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Zhen Ji of Jijun, a man of proven moral character, had withdrawn to Mount Qingyan. When An Lushan became regional commissioner, he recommended Ji as his secretary.

sentences.zh: 濟察祿山有異志，詐得風疾，舁歸家。

translations.literal: Ji perceived that Lushan harbored sinister intent; he pretended to contract wind paralysis and was carried home.
translations.idiomatic: Ji saw that Lushan nursed treasonous ambitions and feigned a paralytic stroke, having himself borne home on a litter.

sentences.zh: 祿山反，使蔡希德引行刑者二人，封刀召之，濟引首待刀，希德以實病白祿山。

translations.literal: When Lushan rebelled, he sent Cai Xide to bring two executioners, with a sealed knife to summon Ji; Ji stretched forth his neck awaiting the blade; Xide reported to Lushan that the illness was genuine.
translations.idiomatic: After Lushan rose in rebellion, he dispatched Cai Xide with two executioners and a sealed blade to fetch Ji. Ji bared his neck for the stroke, but Xide told Lushan that the sickness was real.

sentences.zh: 後安慶緒亦使人強舁至東京，月餘，會廣平王俶平東京，濟起，詣軍門上謁，俶遣詣京師，上命館之於三司，令受賊官爵者列拜以愧其心，以濟為秘書郎。

translations.literal: Later An Qingxu also sent men to force him carried to the Eastern Capital; after more than a month, when Li Chu, Prince of Guangping, pacified the Eastern Capital, Ji rose, went to the army gate to pay respects, Li Chu sent him to the capital, the emperor ordered him lodged at the Three Offices, commanded those who had accepted rebel offices and ranks to line up and bow to shame their hearts, and appointed Ji Secretary Gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: Later An Qingxu had him forcibly carried to the Eastern Capital. More than a month afterward, when Li Chu, Prince of Guangping, recovered the city, Ji rose, presented himself at the camp gate, and was sent on to the capital. Emperor Suzong housed him at the Three Offices and made every official who had taken rebel rank bow before him to sear their conscience, then appointed Ji Secretary Gentleman.

sentences.zh: 國子司業蘇源明稱病不受祿山官，上擢為考功郎中、知制誥。

translations.literal: Su Yuanming, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, claimed illness and did not accept office from Lushan; the emperor promoted him to Director of the Bureau of Evaluations and drafter of edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Su Yuanming, Vice Director of the Directorate of Education, had pleaded illness and refused Lushan's appointment; Emperor Suzong now promoted him to Director of the Bureau of Evaluations with authority to draft imperial proclamations.

sentences.zh: 壬申，上御丹鳳樓，下制：「士庶受賊官祿，為賊用者，令三司條件聞奏；

translations.literal: On day renshen, the emperor ascended the Danfeng Tower and issued an edict: "Commoners and officials who received rebel salaries and were used by the rebels—order the Three Offices to set forth conditions and report;
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen day, Emperor Suzong took the Danfeng Tower and proclaimed: "Subjects who accepted rebel stipends and served the rebels shall be reported to the throne by the Three Offices with particulars;

sentences.zh: 其因戰被虜，或所居密近，因與賊往來者，皆聽自首除罪；

translations.literal: those who because of battle were captured, or whose dwellings lay close by and therefore had dealings with the rebels—all are permitted to confess and be absolved;
translations.idiomatic: those taken captive in battle, or those who lived near rebel-held ground and had dealings with them, may all confess and be pardoned;

sentences.zh: 其子女為賊所污者，勿問。

translations.literal: those whose sons and daughters were defiled by the rebels—do not prosecute.
translations.idiomatic: and no inquiry shall be made where sons or daughters were violated by the rebels."

sentences.zh: 癸酉，回紇葉護自東京還，上命百官迎之於長樂驛，上與宴於宣政殿。

translations.literal: On day guiyou, the Uyghur Yabgu returned from the Eastern Capital; the emperor ordered the hundred officials to welcome him at Changle Post Station, and feasted with him in the Xuanzheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: On the guiyou day, the Uyghur Yabgu came back from the Eastern Capital. Emperor Suzong had the whole court receive him at Changle Post Station and entertained him in the Xuanzheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 葉護奏以「軍中馬少，請留其兵於沙苑，自歸取馬，還為陛下掃除范陽餘孽。

translations.literal: Yabgu memorialized saying, "In the army horses are few; I request to leave my troops at Shayuan, return myself to fetch horses, and come back to sweep away for Your Majesty the remnant rebels of Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yabgu reported that his troops were short of horses, asked to leave his soldiers at Shayuan while he went home to fetch remounts, and promised to return and scour Fanyang clean of the remaining rebels for the emperor.

sentences.zh: 」上賜而遣之。

translations.literal: " The emperor rewarded him and sent him off.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong granted him gifts and let him depart.

sentences.zh: 十一月，廣平王俶、郭子儀來自東京，上勞子儀曰：「吾之家國，由卿再造。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, Li Chu, Prince of Guangping, and Guo Ziyi came from the Eastern Capital; the emperor comforted Ziyi saying, "My house and state were remade by you.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, Li Chu, Prince of Guangping, and Guo Ziyi arrived from the Eastern Capital. Emperor Suzong praised Guo Ziyi: "My dynasty and my realm were reborn through you.

sentences.zh: 張鎬帥魯炅、來瑱、吳王祗、李嗣業、李奐五節度徇河南、河東郡縣，皆下之；

translations.literal: Zhang Hao commanded the five military commissioners Lu Chang, Lai Tian, the Prince of Wu Zhi, Li Siye, and Li Huan to campaign through the commanderies and counties of Henan and Hedong; all submitted;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hao led five commissioners—Lu Chang, Lai Tian, the Prince of Wu Zhi, Li Siye, and Li Huan—through the Henan and Hedong prefectures, and one after another they fell;

sentences.zh: 惟能元皓據北海，高秀巖據大同，未下。

translations.literal: only Neng Yuanhao held Beihai and Gao Xiuyan held Datong—they were not yet taken.
translations.idiomatic: only Neng Yuanhao still held Beihai and Gao Xiuyan Datong.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以回紇葉護為司空、忠義王；

translations.literal: On day jichou, the Uyghur Yabgu was appointed Minister of Works and King of Loyal Righteousness;
translations.idiomatic: On the jichou day, the Uyghur Yabgu was made Minister of Works and enfeoffed as King of Loyal Righteousness;

sentences.zh: 歲遺回紇絹二萬匹，使就朔方軍受之。

translations.literal: each year two ten-thousand bolts of silk were sent to the Uyghurs, with orders to receive them at the Shuofang army.
translations.idiomatic: and every year twenty thousand bolts of silk were sent to the Uyghurs, to be collected from the Shuofang command.

sentences.zh: 以嚴莊為司農卿。

translations.literal: Yan Zhuang was appointed Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhuang was appointed Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 上之在彭原也，更以栗為九廟主；

translations.literal: When the emperor was at Pengyuan, he again used chestnuts as the Nine Temples' offerings;
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Suzong was at Pengyuan, chestnuts had again served as offerings before the ancestral tablets;

sentences.zh: 庚寅，朝享於長樂殿。

translations.literal: On day gengyin, he performed the morning audience and sacrifice in the Changle Hall.
translations.idiomatic: on the gengyin day he conducted the court sacrifice in the Changle Hall.

sentences.zh: 丙申，上皇至鳳翔，從兵六百餘人，上皇命悉以甲兵輸郡庫。

translations.literal: On day bingshen, the Retired Emperor arrived at Fengxiang with more than six hundred followers; the Retired Emperor ordered that all armor and weapons be turned in to the commandery storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: On the bingshen day, Retired Emperor Xuanzong reached Fengxiang with a little over six hundred attendants and ordered every weapon surrendered to the local arsenal.

sentences.zh: 上發精騎三千奉迎。

translations.literal: The emperor dispatched three thousand elite horsemen to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong sent three thousand picked horsemen to meet him.

sentences.zh: 十二月，丙午，上皇至咸陽，上備法駕迎於望賢宮。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on day bingwu, the Retired Emperor reached Xianyang; the emperor prepared the full imperial equipage to welcome him at Wangxian Palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on the bingwu day, Retired Emperor Xuanzong came to Xianyang, where Emperor Suzong met him at Wangxian Palace with the full imperial escort.

sentences.zh: 上皇在宮南樓，上釋黃袍，著紫袍，望樓下馬，趨進，拜舞於樓下。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor was on the south tower of the palace; the emperor removed his yellow robe, put on a purple robe, saw the tower, dismounted from his horse, hurried forward, and performed bowing and dancing obeisance below the tower.
translations.idiomatic: From the palace's south tower the retired emperor looked down as Suzong stripped off his yellow imperial robe, donned a prince's purple, dismounted at sight of the tower, and rushed forward to kowtow below.

sentences.zh: 上皇降樓，撫上而泣。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor descended the tower, stroked the emperor, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong came down the stairs, embraced him, and wept.

sentences.zh: 上捧上皇足，嗚咽不自勝。

translations.literal: The emperor held the Retired Emperor's feet and sobbed beyond control.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong clasped his father's feet and sobbed until he could scarcely breathe.

sentences.zh: 上皇索黃袍，自為上著之，上伏地頓首固辭。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor asked for the yellow robe and himself clothed the emperor in it; the emperor prostrated himself and knocked his head repeatedly, firmly declining.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong called for the yellow robe and dressed him in it himself; Suzong lay prostrate, kowtowing again and again in refusal.

sentences.zh: 上皇曰：「天數、人心皆歸於汝，使朕得保養餘齒，汝之孝也！

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor said, "Heaven's count and men's hearts all return to you; that you enable me to preserve my remaining years—that is your filial piety!
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong said, "Heaven's mandate and the people's hearts are yours. To let me live out my old age in peace—that is filial devotion!

sentences.zh: 」上不得已，受之。

translations.literal: " The emperor had no choice and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: At last Suzong could not refuse and accepted the robe.

sentences.zh: 父老在仗外，歡呼且拜。

translations.literal: The elders of the district were outside the guard of honor, shouting for joy and bowing.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the honor guard the local elders cheered and bowed.

sentences.zh: 上令開仗，縱千餘人入謁上皇，曰：「臣等今日復睹二聖相見，死無恨矣！

translations.literal: The emperor ordered the guard opened and allowed more than a thousand persons to enter and pay respects to the Retired Emperor, saying, "We today again behold the Two Sages meeting—death would hold no regret!
translations.idiomatic: Suzong opened the ranks and admitted more than a thousand people to greet the retired emperor. They cried, "To see the Two Sages reunited today—we can die without regret!

sentences.zh: 」上皇不肯居正殿，曰：「此天子之位也。

translations.literal: " The Retired Emperor would not occupy the main hall, saying, "This is the Son of Heaven's seat.
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong would not take the main hall. "That seat belongs to the Son of Heaven," he said.

sentences.zh: 」上固請，自扶上皇登殿。

translations.literal: " The emperor pressed him firmly and himself supported the Retired Emperor up the steps.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong insisted until he himself helped his father up the steps.

sentences.zh: 尚食進食，上品嚐而薦之。

translations.literal: The Imperial Kitchen presented food; the emperor first tasted it and then offered it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial Kitchen served the meal, Suzong tasted each dish before presenting it to his father.

sentences.zh: 丁未，將發行宮，上親為上皇習馬而進之。

translations.literal: On day dingwei, as they were about to leave the traveling palace, the emperor personally exercised the Retired Emperor's horse and led it forward.
translations.idiomatic: On the dingwei day, before leaving the lodge, Suzong himself walked his father's mount in circles and led it forward.

sentences.zh: 上皇上馬，上親執鞚。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor mounted; the emperor personally held the bridle.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong mounted, Suzong held the reins with his own hands.

sentences.zh: 行數步，上皇止之。

translations.literal: After several paces, the Retired Emperor stopped him.
translations.idiomatic: After a few steps the retired emperor made him stop.

sentences.zh: 上乘馬前引，不敢當馳道。

translations.literal: The emperor mounted his horse and led in front, not daring to occupy the imperial roadway.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong then rode ahead to lead the way, keeping off the imperial carriage road.

sentences.zh: 上皇謂左右曰：「吾為天子五十年，未為貴；

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor said to those beside him, "I was Son of Heaven for fifty years and was not esteemed;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong told his attendants, "I was emperor for fifty years and never felt so honored;

sentences.zh: 今為天子父，乃貴耳！

translations.literal: now as the Son of Heaven's father, only now am I esteemed!
translations.idiomatic: now, as the emperor's father, I am truly exalted!

sentences.zh: 」左右皆呼萬歲。

translations.literal: " Those beside him all shouted "Ten thousand years!"
translations.idiomatic: His attendants shouted "Long live the emperor!"

sentences.zh: 上皇自開遠門入大明宮，御含元殿，慰撫百官；

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor entered the Daming Palace through the Kaiyuan Gate, took the Hanyuan Hall, and comforted the hundred officials;
translations.idiomatic: Xuanzong entered the Daming Palace through the Kaiyuan Gate, took the Hanyuan Hall, and reassured the officials;

sentences.zh: 乃詣長東殿謝九廟主，慟哭久之；

translations.literal: then went to the Changdong Hall to pay respects before the Nine Temples' tablets, wailing long;
translations.idiomatic: then went to the Changdong Hall to bow before the ancestral tablets and wept for a long while;

sentences.zh: 即日，幸興慶宮，遂居之。

translations.literal: that same day he visited the Xingqing Palace and thereafter dwelt there.
translations.idiomatic: that same day he moved into the Xingqing Palace and made it his residence.

sentences.zh: 上累表請避位還東宮，上皇不許。

translations.literal: The emperor repeatedly memorialized requesting to yield the throne and return to the Eastern Palace; the Retired Emperor did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: Suzong repeatedly asked to abdicate and return to the Eastern Palace, but Xuanzong would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，以禮部尚書李峴、兵部侍郎呂諲為詳理使，與御史大夫崔器共按陳希烈等獄。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, Li Xian, Minister of Rites, and Lü Zhen, Vice Minister of War, were made commissioners for detailed review, and together with Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi jointly investigated the cases of Chen Xilie and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinhai day, Li Xian, Minister of Rites, and Lü Zhen, Vice Minister of War, were appointed commissioners for detailed review to join Censor-in-Chief Cui Qi in trying the cases of Chen Xilie and his fellows.

sentences.zh: 峴以殿中侍御史李棲筠為詳理判官，棲筠多務平恕，故人皆怨諲、器之刻深，而峴獨得美譽。

translations.literal: Li Xian appointed Palace Censor Li Qiyun as reviewing judge; Qiyun for the most part strove for leniency and forgiveness, so people all resented Lü Zhen and Cui Qi's severity, while Li Xian alone won fine reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian named Palace Censor Li Qiyun as reviewing judge. Qiyun leaned toward mercy, so public resentment fell on Lü Zhen and Cui Qi for their harshness while Li Xian alone won praise.

sentences.zh: 戊午，上御丹鳳樓，赦天下，惟與安祿山同反及李林甫、王鉷、楊國忠子孫不在免例。

translations.literal: On day wuwu, the emperor ascended the Danfeng Tower and amnestied the realm; only those who rebelled together with An Lushan and the descendants of Li Linfu, Wang Hong, and Yang Guozhong were outside the exemption.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day, Emperor Suzong took the Danfeng Tower and proclaimed a general amnesty, exempting only those who had risen with An Lushan and the descendants of Li Linfu, Wang Hong, and Yang Guozhong.

sentences.zh: 立廣平王俶為楚王，加郭子儀司徒，李光弼司空，自餘蜀郡、靈武扈從立功之臣，皆進階，賜爵，加食邑有差。

translations.literal: Li Chu, Prince of Guangping, was established as Prince of Chu; Guo Ziyi was advanced to Minister of Education, Li Guangbi to Minister of Works; from the rest, the meritorious followers who had accompanied the emperor to Shu and Lingwu—all were promoted in rank, granted noble titles, and given increased food fiefs in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chu, Prince of Guangping, was created Prince of Chu; Guo Ziyi was made Minister of Education and Li Guangbi Minister of Works; and every other minister who had followed the court to Shu and Lingwu was promoted, ennobled, and granted enlarged fiefs according to merit.

sentences.zh: 李憕、盧奕、顏杲卿、袁履謙、許遠、張巡、張介然、蔣清、龐堅等皆加追贈，官其子孫。

translations.literal: Li Qian, Lu Yi, Yan Gaoqing, Yuan Lüqian, Xu Yuan, Zhang Xun, Zhang Jieran, Jiang Qing, Pang Jian, and the rest were all given posthumous honors, and their sons and grandsons were appointed to office.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qian, Lu Yi, Yan Gaoqing, Yuan Lüqian, Xu Yuan, Zhang Xun, Zhang Jieran, Jiang Qing, Pang Jian, and others received posthumous honors, and their sons and grandsons were given official appointments.

sentences.zh: 戰亡之家，給復二載。

translations.literal: Families of those who died in battle were granted two years' tax exemption.
translations.idiomatic: Families of the war dead were exempted from levies for two years.

sentences.zh: 郡縣來載租、庸三分蠲一。

translations.literal: For the land tax and corvée delivered by the commanderies and counties in the coming year, one-third was remitted.
translations.idiomatic: Land tax and corvée payments due from the commanderies in the coming year were cut by one-third.

sentences.zh: 近所改郡名、官名，一依故事。

translations.literal: Recently changed commandery names and office titles—all were restored according to precedent.
