translations.idiomatic: Commandery and office titles changed during the rebellion were all restored to their former names.

sentences.zh: 以蜀郡為南京，鳳翔為西京，西京為中京。

translations.literal: Shu Commandery was made the Southern Capital, Fengxiang the Western Capital, and the former Western Capital the Central Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shu was named the Southern Capital, Fengxiang the Western Capital, and the old Western Capital became the Central Capital.

sentences.zh: 以張良娣為淑妃，立皇子南陽王人系為趙王，新城王僅為彭王，穎川王僩為兗王，東陽王侹為涇王，璜為襄王，倕為杞王，偲為召王，昭為興王，侗為定王。

translations.literal: Consort Zhang Liangdi was made Shufei; the princes were established—the Prince of Nanyang Renxi as Prince of Zhao, the Prince of Xincheng Jin as Prince of Peng, the Prince of Yingchuan Dan as Prince of Yan, the Prince of Dongyang Ting as Prince of Jing, Huang as Prince of Xiang, Chui as Prince of Qi, Si as Prince of Shao, Zhao as Prince of Xing, and Tong as Prince of Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Consort Zhang Liangdi was raised to Shufei, and the imperial sons were enfeoffed: Renxi, Prince of Nanyang, as Prince of Zhao; Jin, Prince of Xincheng, as Prince of Peng; Dan, Prince of Yingchuan, as Prince of Yan; Ting, Prince of Dongyang, as Prince of Jing; Huang as Prince of Xiang; Chui as Prince of Qi; Si as Prince of Shao; Zhao as Prince of Xing; and Tong as Prince of Ding.

sentences.zh: 議者或罪張巡以守睢陽不去，與其食人，曷若全人。

translations.literal: Some in debate blamed Zhang Xun for holding Suiyang and not leaving—for eating men rather than preserving men.
translations.idiomatic: Some critics condemned Zhang Xun for holding Suiyang to the end: by eating the dead, they argued, he had destroyed lives he might have saved.

sentences.zh: 其友人李翰為之作傳，表上之，以為：「巡以寡擊眾，以弱制強，保江、淮以待陛下之師，師至而巡死，巡之功大矣。

translations.literal: His friend Li Han wrote a biography for him and submitted it as a memorial, stating: "Xun with few struck many, with weak controlled strong, guarded the Yangtze and Huai to await Your Majesty's armies—the armies arrived and Xun died; Xun's achievement was great.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Li Han wrote his biography and presented it to the throne, arguing: "With a handful Xun fought multitudes; with the weak he mastered the strong. He shielded the Yangtze and Huai until Your Majesty's armies could come. The armies arrived only after Xun had died—his service was immense.

sentences.zh: 而議者或罪巡以食人，愚巡以守死，善遏惡揚，錄瑕棄用，臣竊痛之！

translations.literal: Yet some in debate blame Xun for eating men, deem Xun foolish for dying in defense, curb the good and spread the evil, record the flaw and discard the use—I privately grieve at this!
translations.idiomatic: Yet some blame him for cannibalism, as though devotion unto death were folly—suppressing virtue to broadcast vice, seizing on a stain and discarding his worth. This pains me deeply.

sentences.zh: 巡所以固守者，以待諸軍之救，救不至而食盡，食既盡而及人，乖其素志。

translations.literal: The reason Xun so firmly held was to await rescue by the various armies; rescue did not arrive and food was exhausted; when food was exhausted it reached men—contrary to his constant intent.
translations.idiomatic: He held the city to await relief. Relief never came; provisions ran out; when nothing remained, hunger drove men to the unthinkable—far from what he had ever intended.

sentences.zh: 設使巡守城之初已有食人之計，損數百之眾以全天下，臣猶曰功過相掩，況非其素志乎！

translations.literal: Suppose that at the beginning of Xun's defense of the city he already had a plan to eat men, sacrificing several hundred lives to preserve the realm—I would still say merit and fault offset each other; how much more when it was not his constant intent!
translations.idiomatic: Even if he had planned from the first to sacrifice hundreds to save the empire, I would still call merit and fault a fair trade—how much more so when that was never his purpose!

sentences.zh: 今巡死大難，不睹休明，唯其令名是其榮祿。

translations.literal: Now Xun died in great calamity, did not behold the age of glory—only his fine name is his honor and emolument.
translations.idiomatic: Xun perished in the catastrophe and never saw the restoration; a good name is now his only reward.

sentences.zh: 若不時紀錄，恐遠而不傳，使巡生死不遇，誠可悲焉！

translations.literal: If he is not recorded in timely fashion, I fear distant ages will not transmit it, making Xun unmet in life and death—truly pitiable!
translations.idiomatic: Unless his deeds are set down now, they may never reach posterity, and he would be wronged in life and death alike—a grievous loss.

sentences.zh: 臣敢撰傳一卷獻上，乞編列史官。

translations.literal: Your servant ventures to compose one scroll of biography and present it, begging that it be entered among the historiographers.
translations.idiomatic: I humbly submit this biography and ask that the historians enroll it in the official record.

sentences.zh: 」眾議由是始息。

translations.literal: " Public debate thereby first subsided.
translations.idiomatic: The controversy then began to die away.

sentences.zh: 是後赦令無不及李憕等，而程千里獨以生執賊庭，不沾褒贈。

translations.literal: Thereafter amnesty edicts none failed to reach Li Qian and the rest, yet Cheng Qianli alone, because he was captured alive in the rebel court, received no commendation or reward.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward every amnesty honored men such as Li Qian, yet Cheng Qianli alone—taken alive in the rebel camp—received no posthumous praise.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上皇御宣政殿，以傳國寶授上，上始涕泣而受之。

translations.literal: On day jiazi, the Retired Emperor took the Xuanzheng Hall and handed the heirloom jade seal to the emperor; the emperor for the first time received it weeping.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiazi day, Retired Emperor Xuanzong presided in the Xuanzheng Hall and passed the imperial seal to Suzong, who accepted it at last with tears.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒之北走也，其大將北平王李歸仁及精兵曳落河、同羅、六州胡數萬人皆潰歸范陽，所過俘掠，人物無遺。

translations.literal: When An Qingxu fled north, his great general Li Guiren, Prince of Northern Ping, and elite troops—the Yeluohe, Tongluo, and Six-States Hu, several tens of thousands—all collapsed and returned to Fanyang; wherever they passed they seized booty, leaving no person or thing behind.
translations.idiomatic: As An Qingxu fled north, his general Li Guiren, Prince of Northern Ping, and tens of thousands of elite Yeluohe, Tongluo, and Six-States Hu troops broke up and streamed back toward Fanyang, plundering everything in their path until nothing remained.

sentences.zh: 史思明厚為之備，且遣使逆招之范陽境，曳落河、六州胡皆降。

translations.literal: Shi Siming made lavish preparations for them and also sent envoys ahead to welcome and recruit them at the Fanyang border; the Yeluohe and Six-States Hu all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming made lavish preparations and sent envoys to meet them at the Fanyang frontier; the Yeluohe and Six-States Hu submitted to him.

sentences.zh: 同羅不從，思明縱兵擊之，同羅大敗，悉奪其所掠，餘眾走歸其國。

translations.literal: The Tongluo did not follow; Siming unleashed troops to strike them; the Tongluo were greatly defeated, all their plunder was seized, and the remnant host fled back to their state.
translations.idiomatic: The Tongluo refused. Siming attacked them, routed them utterly, seized all they had looted, and drove the survivors back to their homeland.

sentences.zh: 慶緒忌思明之強，遣阿史那承慶、安守忠往徵兵，因密圖之。

translations.literal: Qingxu resented Siming's strength and dispatched Ashina Chengqing and An Shouzhong to levy troops, while secretly plotting against him.
translations.idiomatic: An Qingxu, jealous of Siming's power, sent Ashina Chengqing and An Shouzhong to summon his troops while secretly plotting his downfall.

sentences.zh: 判官耿仁智說思明曰：「大夫崇重，人莫敢言，仁智願一言而死。

translations.literal: Judge Geng Renzhi urged Siming saying, "The Grandee is held in high honor and none dare speak; Renzhi would speak one word even at the cost of death.
translations.idiomatic: His aide Geng Renzhi urged him: "You stand too high for anyone to speak plainly. I will speak even if it costs my life.

sentences.zh: 」思明曰：「何也？

translations.literal: " Siming said, "What is it?
translations.idiomatic: Siming asked, "What is it?

sentences.zh: 」仁智曰：「大夫所以盡力於安氏者，迫於凶威耳，今唐室中興，天子仁聖，大夫誠帥所部歸之，此轉禍為福之計也。

translations.literal: " Renzhi said, "The reason the Grandee exerted all strength for the An house was only compelled by fierce might; now the Tang house is reviving, the Son of Heaven is benevolent and sage—if the Grandee truly leads his detachments to return to them, this is the plan to turn calamity into blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Geng Renzhi replied, "You served the An clan only because their terror forced you. The Tang is rising again and the emperor is merciful. Lead your troops back to the throne—that is how you turn disaster into fortune.

sentences.zh: 」裨將烏承玼說思明曰：「今唐室再造，慶緒葉上露耳。

translations.literal: " Deputy general Wu Chengzhen urged Siming saying, "Now the Tang house is remade; Qingxu is but dew on a leaf.
translations.idiomatic: His deputy Wu Chengzhen added, "The Tang has been remade. Qingxu is dew on a leaf.

sentences.zh: 大夫奈何與之俱亡！

translations.literal: How can the Grandee perish together with him!
translations.idiomatic: Why should you perish with him?

sentences.zh: 若歸款朝廷，以自湔洗，易於反掌耳。

translations.literal: If you return allegiance to the court to cleanse yourself, it is easier than turning the palm.
translations.idiomatic: Submit to the court and wash yourself clean—it is easier than turning your hand over.

sentences.zh: 」思明以為然。

translations.literal: " Siming thought it right.
translations.idiomatic: Siming agreed.

sentences.zh: 承慶、守忠以五千勁騎自隨，至范陽，思明番眾數萬迎之，相距一里所，使人謂承慶等曰：「相公及王遠至，將士不勝其喜，然邊兵怯懦，懼相公之眾，不敢進，願弛弓以安之。

translations.literal: Chengqing and Shouzhong had five thousand crack horsemen accompany them; reaching Fanyang, Siming's tribal hosts of several tens of thousands welcomed them, standing about a li apart; he sent men to tell Chengqing and the rest, "The Chancellor and the Prince have come from afar; the soldiers cannot contain their joy, yet the border troops are timid and fear the Chancellor's host, not daring to advance—we beg you unstring your bows to reassure them.
translations.idiomatic: Chengqing and Shouzhong arrived with five thousand picked horsemen. At Fanyang, Siming's tribal warriors—tens of thousands strong—met them a li away and sent word: "Your lordships have come far, and our men rejoice, but the frontier troops are timid before your numbers. Unstring your bows so they may be at ease.

sentences.zh: 」承慶等從之。

translations.literal: " Chengqing and the rest complied.
translations.idiomatic: They did so.

sentences.zh: 思明引承慶等入內廳樂飲，別遣人收其甲兵，諸郡兵皆給糧縱遣之，願留者厚賜，分隸諸營。

translations.literal: Siming led Chengqing and the rest into the inner hall for music and drinking, separately sent men to collect their armor and weapons; troops from the various commanderies were all given grain and released, those wishing to stay were richly rewarded and distributed among the various camps.
translations.idiomatic: Siming ushered them into the inner hall for a feast, while others quietly collected their arms. He fed the provincial soldiers, released those who wished to go, richly rewarded those who stayed, and assigned them to his camps.

sentences.zh: 明日。

translations.literal: The next day.
translations.idiomatic: The next day,

sentences.zh: 囚承慶等，遣其將竇子昂奉表以所部十三郡及兵八萬來降，並帥其河東節度使高秀巖亦以所部來降。

translations.literal: he imprisoned Chengqing and the rest, sent his general Dou Zi'ang to present a memorial offering the thirteen commanderies under his command and eighty thousand troops in surrender, and also led his Hedong commissioner Gao Xiuyan to surrender his detachments as well.
translations.idiomatic: he imprisoned Chengqing and his party, and sent his general Dou Zi'ang with a memorial offering thirteen commanderies and eighty thousand men in surrender, while his Hedong commissioner Gao Xiuyan submitted his forces as well.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，子昂至京師。

translations.literal: On day yichou, Zi'ang reached the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the yichou day, Dou Zi'ang reached the capital.

sentences.zh: 上大喜，以思明為歸義王、范陽節度使，子七人皆除顯官。

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly pleased, appointed Siming King of Returning Righteousness and Fanyang military commissioner, and all seven of his sons were given eminent offices.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong was overjoyed, made Siming King of Returning Allegiance and military commissioner of Fanyang, and gave lofty posts to all seven of his sons.

sentences.zh: 遣內侍李思敬與烏承恩往宣慰，使將所部兵討慶緒。

translations.literal: He dispatched the inner attendant Li Sijing and Wu Chengen to proclaim comfort, ordering them to lead the troops under their command to attack Qingxu.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the eunuch Li Sijing with Wu Chengen to announce the court's favor and ordered them to lead Siming's troops against An Qingxu.

sentences.zh: 先是，慶緒以張忠志為常山太守，思明召忠志還范陽，以其將薛萼攝恆州刺史，開井陘路，招趙郡太守陸濟，降之；

translations.literal: Earlier, Qingxu had appointed Zhang Zhongzhi as Changshan prefect; Siming summoned Zhongzhi back to Fanyang, had his general Xue E act as Hengzhou inspector, opened the Jingxing road, recruited Zhao Commandery prefect Lu Ji, and received his surrender;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, An Qingxu had made Zhang Zhongzhi prefect of Changshan. Siming recalled Zhongzhi to Fanyang, put his general Xue E in charge of Hengzhou, opened the Jingxing route, and won over Lu Ji, prefect of Zhao Commandery;

sentences.zh: 命其子朝義將兵五千人攝冀州刺史，以其將令狐彰為博州刺史。

translations.literal: he ordered his son Chaoyi to command five thousand troops as acting Jizhou inspector, and his general Linghu Zhang as Bozhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: he sent his son Chaoyi with five thousand men to hold Jizhou and appointed his general Linghu Zhang prefect of Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 烏承恩所至宣佈詔旨，滄、瀛、安、深、德、棣等州皆降，雖相州未下，河北率為唐有矣。

translations.literal: Wherever Wu Chengen went he proclaimed the imperial edict; Cang, Ying, An, Shen, De, Di, and other prefectures all surrendered; although Xiangzhou was not yet taken, for the most part Hebei belonged to the Tang.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Wu Chengen went he proclaimed the imperial edicts, and Cang, Ying, An, Shen, De, Di, and the other prefectures submitted. Although Xiangzhou still held out, Hebei was largely Tang territory again.

sentences.zh: 上皇加上尊號曰光天文武大聖孝感皇帝。

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor was given the elevated title Emperor of Luminous Heaven, Civil and Martial, Great Sage, Great Filial Feeling.
translations.idiomatic: Retired Emperor Xuanzong was given the honorific title Emperor of Luminous Heaven, Civil and Martial, Great Sage, and Great Filial Piety.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀還東都，經營河北。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi returned to the Eastern Capital and organized affairs in Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi returned to the Eastern Capital to organize the recovery of Hebei.

sentences.zh: 崔器、呂諲上言：「諸陷賊官，背國從偽，准律皆應處死。

translations.literal: Cui Qi and Lü Zhen submitted saying, "All officials who fell into rebel hands, turned their backs on the state and followed the false ruler—according to law all should be put to death.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qi and Lü Zhen memorialized: "Every official who served under the rebels betrayed the state and followed a usurper; by law they all deserve death.

sentences.zh: 」上欲從之。

translations.literal: " The emperor wished to follow this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong was inclined to agree.

sentences.zh: 李峴以為：「賊陷兩京，天子南巡，人自逃生。

translations.literal: Li Xian held that: "The rebels seized the two capitals, the Son of Heaven toured south, and each man saved himself as he could.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xian argued: "When the rebels took both capitals and the Son of Heaven withdrew south, every man fled to save himself.

sentences.zh: 此屬皆陛下親戚或勳舊子孫，今一概以叛法處死，恐乖仁恕之道。

translations.literal: These people are all Your Majesty's kin or descendants of meritorious ministers; now to put them all to death under the law of rebellion— I fear this strays from the way of benevolence and forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: They are all Your Majesty's relatives or the descendants of meritorious ministers. To execute every one of them under the law of rebellion would betray the way of mercy and forbearance.

sentences.zh: 且河北未平，群臣陷賊者尚多，若寬之，足開自新之路；

translations.literal: Moreover, Hebei is not yet pacified, and many among the ministers who fell into rebel hands remain; if they are treated leniently, that is enough to open a path of self-renewal;
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, Hebei is not yet pacified, and many officials who served under the rebels are still out there. If we show leniency, we open a path for them to reform.

sentences.zh: 若盡誅之，是堅其附賊之心也。

translations.literal: if all are put to death, this hardens their hearts in attachment to the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: If we execute them all, we only harden their resolve to stay with the rebels.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：『殲厥渠魁，脅從罔理。

translations.literal: The Documents say: "Destroy their ringleaders; the coerced followers are not to be prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Destroy the ringleaders; do not punish those who were coerced into following them."

sentences.zh: 』諲、器守文，不達大體。

translations.literal: " Zhen and Qi cling to the letter of the law and do not grasp the larger design.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Zhen and Cui Qi cling to the letter of the law and miss the larger design.

sentences.zh: 惟陛上圖之。

translations.literal: May Your Majesty consider it.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to weigh this carefully.

sentences.zh: 」爭之累日，上從峴議，以六等定罪，重者刑之於市，次賜自盡，次重杖一百，次三等流、貶。

translations.literal: " They argued for many days; the emperor followed Xian's proposal, fixed guilt in six grades—the gravest were executed in the market, next were granted suicide, next were given one hundred heavy strokes of the staff, and the three lowest grades were banished or demoted.
translations.idiomatic: They argued for days. The emperor accepted Li Xian's proposal and divided the guilty into six grades: the gravest were executed in public; the next rank were permitted to take their own lives; the next received one hundred strokes of the heavy staff; and the three lowest grades were exiled or demoted.

sentences.zh: 壬申，斬達奚珣等十八人於城西南獨柳樹下，陳希烈等七人賜自盡於大理寺；

translations.literal: On day renshen, Daxi Xun and eighteen others were beheaded beneath the Solitary Willow southwest of the city; Chen Xilie and seven others were granted suicide at the Court of Judicial Review;
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Daxi Xun and eighteen others were beheaded beneath the Solitary Willow southwest of the city, while Chen Xilie and seven others were permitted to kill themselves at the Court of Judicial Review;

sentences.zh: 應受杖者於京兆府門。

translations.literal: those who were to receive the staff were punished at the gate of the Jingzhao prefectural office.
translations.idiomatic: those sentenced to the staff were beaten at the gate of the Jingzhao prefectural office.

sentences.zh: 上欲免張均、張垍死，上皇曰：「均、垍事賊，皆任權要。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to spare Zhang Jun and Zhang Ji from death; the Retired Emperor said: "Jun and Ji served the rebels and both held weighty power.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to spare Zhang Jun and Zhang Ji from death. The Retired Emperor said: "Jun and Ji served the rebels and both held positions of great power.

sentences.zh: 均仍為賊毀吾家事，罪不可赦！

translations.literal: Jun moreover worked for the rebels to ruin my household affairs—the crime cannot be pardoned!
translations.idiomatic: Jun even helped the rebels destroy my household—his crime cannot be forgiven!

sentences.zh: 」上叩頭再拜曰：「臣非張說父子，無有今日。

translations.literal: " The emperor knocked his head and bowed twice, saying: "Had it not been for Zhang Yue and his sons, your servant would not have this day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor kowtowed and said: "Without Zhang Yue and his sons, I would not be emperor today.

sentences.zh: 臣不能活均、垍，使死者有知，何面目見說於九泉！

translations.literal: Your servant cannot keep Jun and Ji alive; if the dead have awareness, with what face could I meet Yue in the nine springs!
translations.idiomatic: If I cannot save Jun and Ji, and the dead have awareness, how could I face Yue in the grave!

sentences.zh: 」因俯伏流涕。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he prostrated himself and wept.
translations.idiomatic: He prostrated himself, weeping.

sentences.zh: 上皇命左右扶上起，曰：「張垍為汝長流嶺表，張均必不可活，汝更勿救！

translations.literal: The Retired Emperor ordered attendants to help the emperor rise and said: "Zhang Ji, for your sake, shall be exiled far to Lingnan; Zhang Jun absolutely cannot live—do not plead for him again!
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor had attendants raise him and said: "For your sake Zhang Ji shall be exiled to the far south, but Zhang Jun must die—do not plead for him again!"

sentences.zh: 」上泣而從命。

translations.literal: " The emperor wept and obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and obeyed.

sentences.zh: 安祿山所署河南尹張萬頃獨以在賊中能保庇百姓，不坐。

translations.literal: Zhang Wanqing, whom An Lushan had appointed Henan intendant, alone because while among the rebels he could protect and shelter the common people, was not prosecuted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wanqing, whom An Lushan had appointed Henan intendant, alone escaped prosecution because he had sheltered the people while serving under the rebels.

sentences.zh: 頃之，有自賊中來降者，言「唐群臣從安慶緒在鄴者，聞廣平王赦陳希烈等，皆自悼，恨失身賊庭；

translations.literal: Before long, one who had surrendered from among the rebels said: "Tang ministers following An Qingxu at Ye, hearing that the Prince of Guangping had pardoned Chen Xilie and the rest, all lamented themselves and regretted having lost their persons in the rebel court;
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward a man who had defected from the rebels reported: "The Tang officials with An Qingxu at Ye, hearing that Prince of Guangping Li Chu had pardoned Chen Xilie and the others, all grieved that they had thrown their lives away in the rebel court;

sentences.zh: 及聞希烈等誅，乃止。

translations.literal: when they heard that Xilie and the rest had been executed, they then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: when they heard that Xilie and the others had been executed, they abandoned the idea."

sentences.zh: 」上甚悔之。

translations.literal: " The emperor deeply regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor deeply regretted his decision.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：為人臣者，策名委質，有死無貳。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: One who serves as a minister registers his name and commits his person—there is death but no second allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: A minister registers his name and pledges his person to his lord; he may die, but he must not serve two masters.

sentences.zh: 希烈等或貴為卿相，或親連肺腑，於承平之日，無一言以規人主之失，救社稷之危，迎合取容以竊富貴；

translations.literal: Xilie and the rest were either exalted as ministers and chancellors or closely linked by flesh and bone; in days of peace they had not a single word to admonish the ruler's faults and rescue the altars of state from peril, but fawned for favor to steal wealth and rank;
translations.idiomatic: Men like Chen Xilie were either exalted as chancellors or bound to the throne by kinship, yet in peaceful times they never spoke to correct the ruler's faults or save the state from peril; they fawned for favor and stole rank and riches;

sentences.zh: 及四海橫潰，乘輿播越，偷生苟免，顧戀妻子，媚賊稱臣，為之陳力，此乃屠酤之所羞，犬馬之不如。

translations.literal: when the four seas collapsed in ruin and the imperial carriage was driven into exile, they stole life and sought bare escape, clinging to wife and children, fawning on the rebels and calling themselves subjects, offering their strength on the rebels' behalf—this is what butchers and wine-sellers would be ashamed of, worse than dogs and horses.
translations.idiomatic: when the realm collapsed and the Son of Heaven fled, they clung to life, doted on wives and children, fawned on the rebels and called themselves their subjects, and served them with all their strength—conduct that butchers and tavernkeepers would despise, beneath even dogs and horses.

sentences.zh: 倘更全其首領，復其官爵，是謅諛之臣無往而不得計也。

translations.literal: If moreover their heads and necks were spared and their offices and titles restored, then fawning, flattering ministers would have nowhere they could not carry out their schemes.
translations.idiomatic: If they were spared and restored to office, every sycophant in the realm would know that treachery pays.

sentences.zh: 彼顏杲卿、張巡之徒，世治則擯斥外方，沉抑下僚；

translations.literal: Those such as Yan Gaoqing and Zhang Xun—in an age of order were cast out to distant posts and held down in low offices;
translations.idiomatic: Men like Yan Gaoqing and Zhang Xun, in times of peace, were shunted to distant posts and kept in low rank;

sentences.zh: 世亂則委棄孤城，齏粉寇手。

translations.literal: in an age of chaos were abandoned in lone cities and ground to powder in the enemy's hands.
translations.idiomatic: in times of chaos they were left to defend forsaken cities and were ground to dust by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 何為善者之不幸而為惡者之幸，朝廷待忠義之薄而保奸邪之厚邪！

translations.literal: Why is it that the good are unfortunate while the wicked are fortunate, that the court treats loyalty and righteousness thinly yet preserves the wicked and depraved thickly!
translations.idiomatic: Why must the good suffer misfortune while the wicked prosper? Why does the court treat loyalty so thinly and shelter treachery so generously!

sentences.zh: 至於微賤之臣，巡徼之隸，謀議不預，號令不及，朝聞親征之詔，夕失警蹕之所，乃復責其不能扈從，不亦難哉！

translations.literal: As for humble, lowly ministers and patrol guards on the frontiers, who took no part in counsel and whom orders did not reach—in the morning they heard the edict for the ruler's personal campaign, and by evening they had lost the place of the imperial guard—yet they were again blamed for failing to escort him: is this not too hard!
translations.idiomatic: As for humble officials and frontier patrolmen who had no voice in counsel and received no orders—in the morning they heard that the emperor was marching in person, and by evening the imperial guard had vanished—yet they were blamed for failing to escort him. Was that not asking the impossible!

sentences.zh: 六等議刑，斯亦可矣，又何悔焉！

translations.literal: The six-grade deliberation on punishments was adequate enough—why regret it!
translations.idiomatic: The six-grade scheme of punishments was punishment enough. Why regret it!

sentences.zh: 故妃韋氏既廢為尼，居禁中，是歲卒。

translations.literal: The former consort of the Wei clan, having been deposed and made a nun, dwelt within the forbidden precincts; this year she died.
translations.idiomatic: The former consort Lady Wei, deposed and made a nun, lived within the palace precincts; she died that year.

sentences.zh: 置左、右神武軍，取元從子弟充，其制皆如四軍，總謂之北牙六軍。

translations.literal: The Left and Right Divine Martial Armies were established, filled with sons and younger brothers of the original followers; their regulations were all like the four armies, and in total they were called the Northern Gate Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: The Left and Right Divine Martial Armies were established, staffed with sons of the emperor's original followers; their organization matched the four existing armies, and together they were called the Northern Gate Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 又擇善騎射者千人為殿前射生手，分左、右廂，號曰英武軍。

translations.literal: Again, one thousand skilled in riding and archery were chosen as Palace Front Archery Guards, divided into left and right wings, titled the Valiant Martial Army.
translations.idiomatic: A thousand skilled horsemen and archers were also chosen as Palace Front Archery Guards, divided into left and right wings, and called the Valiant Martial Army.

sentences.zh: 升河中防禦使為節度，領蒲、絳等七州；

translations.literal: The Hezhong defense commissioner was promoted to military commissioner, governing Pu, Jiang, and six other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: The Hezhong defense commissioner was promoted to a full military commission over Pu, Jiang, and six other prefectures;

sentences.zh: 分劍南為東、西川節度，東川領梓、遂等十二州；

translations.literal: Jiannan was divided into Eastern and Western Chuan military commissions; Eastern Chuan governed Zi, Sui, and eleven other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Jiannan was split into Eastern and Western Chuan commissions; Eastern Chuan governed Zi, Sui, and eleven other prefectures;

sentences.zh: 又置荊澧節度，領荊、澧等五州；

translations.literal: a Jing-Li military commission was also established, governing Jing, Li, and three other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: a Jing-Li commission was added over Jing, Li, and three other prefectures;

sentences.zh: 夔峽節度，領夔、峽等五州；

translations.literal: a Kui-Xia military commission governed Kui, Xia, and three other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: and a Kui-Xia commission over Kui, Xia, and three other prefectures;

sentences.zh: 更安西曰鎮西。

translations.literal: Anxi was renamed Zhenxi.
translations.idiomatic: Anxi was renamed Zhenxi.

sentences.zh: 肅宗文明武德大聖大宣孝皇帝中之下乾元元年（

translations.literal: The middle section, lower portion, of Emperor Suzong the Civil, Cultured, Martial, Virtuous, Great Sage, Great Proclaimer of Filial Piety, first year of Qianyuan (
translations.idiomatic: In the latter portion of the reign of Emperor Suzong, first year of Qianyuan (

sentences.zh: 戊戌，公元七五八年）

translations.literal: wuxu, year 758 CE)
translations.idiomatic: wuxu, 758 CE)

sentences.zh: 春，正月，戊寅，上皇御宣政殿，授冊，加上尊號。

translations.literal: Spring, first month, day wuyin: the Retired Emperor took the Xuanzheng Hall, received the investiture document, and was given an honorific title.
translations.idiomatic: In spring, the first month, on wuyin the Retired Emperor entered the Xuanzheng Hall to receive the investiture scroll and an honorific title.

sentences.zh: 上固辭「大聖」之號，上皇不許。

translations.literal: The emperor firmly declined the title "Great Sage"; the Retired Emperor would not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor firmly declined the epithet "Great Sage," but the Retired Emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 上尊上皇曰太上至道聖皇天帝。

translations.literal: The emperor honored the Retired Emperor as Supreme Sovereign, Utmost Way, Sage Emperor, Heavenly Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: He honored the Retired Emperor as Supreme Sovereign, Utmost Way, Sage Emperor, Heavenly Emperor.

sentences.zh: 先是，官軍既克京城，宗廟之器及府庫資財多散在民間，遣使檢括，頗有煩擾；

translations.literal: Earlier, after the government armies had taken the capital, ritual vessels of the ancestral temples and treasury goods and wealth had largely scattered among the populace; envoys were sent to search and recover them, and there was considerable harassment;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the imperial armies recaptured the capital, ancestral temple vessels and treasury goods had scattered among the people; envoys sent to recover them caused considerable harassment;

sentences.zh: 乙酉，敕盡停之，乃命京兆尹李峴安撫坊市。

translations.literal: on day yiyou an edict halted all of this entirely, and Li Xian, intendant of Jingzhao, was ordered to pacify and reassure the wards and markets.
translations.idiomatic: on yiyou an edict halted the searches entirely, and Li Xian, intendant of Jingzhao, was ordered to pacify the wards and markets.

sentences.zh: 二月，癸卯朔，以殿中監李輔國兼太僕卿。

translations.literal: Second month, first day guimao: Li Fuguo, palace director, was made concurrent Grand Master of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month, on the first day guimao, Palace Director Li Fuguo was also appointed Grand Master of the Stud.

sentences.zh: 輔國依附張淑妃，判元帥府行軍司馬，勢傾朝野。

translations.literal: Fuguo relied on Consort Zhang Shu, served as acting marshal's headquarters march chief of staff, and his power tilted court and commonwealth.
translations.idiomatic: Fuguo relied on Consort Zhang Shu, served as acting chief of staff of the supreme commander's headquarters, and his power dominated the court.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒所署北海節度使能元皓舉所部來降，以為鴻臚卿，充河北招討使。

translations.literal: Neng Yuanhao, whom An Qingxu had appointed Beihai military commissioner, led his entire command in surrender; he was made Minister Herald and charged as Hebei pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Neng Yuanhao, whom An Qingxu had appointed Beihai military commissioner, surrendered with his entire command; he was made Minister Herald and charged with pacifying Hebei.

sentences.zh: 丁未，上御明鳳門，赦天下，改元。

translations.literal: On day dingwei the emperor took the Mingfeng Gate, amnestied the realm, and changed the reign title.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei the emperor appeared at the Mingfeng Gate, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the reign title.

sentences.zh: 盡免百姓今載租、庸。

translations.literal: All land tax and corvée labor for the common people of this year were entirely remitted.
translations.idiomatic: All land tax and corvée for the year were remitted.

sentences.zh: 復以載為年。

translations.literal: The character zai was restored for naming the year.
translations.idiomatic: The character zai was restored for use in dating the year.

sentences.zh: 庚午，以安東副大都護王玄志為營州刺史，充平盧節度使。

translations.literal: On day gengwu Wang Xuanzhi, vice protector-general of Andong, was made prefect of Yingzhou and commissioned as Pinglu military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Wang Xuanzhi, vice protector-general of Andong, was appointed prefect of Yingzhou and military commissioner of Pinglu.

sentences.zh: 三月，甲戌，徙楚王俶為成王。

translations.literal: Third month, day jiaxu: Prince of Chu Chu was moved to Prince of Cheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on jiaxu, Prince of Chu Li Chu was redesignated Prince of Cheng.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，立張淑妃為皇后。

translations.literal: On day wuyin Consort Zhang Shu was established as empress.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin Consort Zhang Shu was made empress.

sentences.zh: 鎮西、北庭行營節度使李嗣業屯河內。

translations.literal: Li Siye, military commissioner of the Zhenxi and Beiting field headquarters, encamped at Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siye, military commissioner of the Zhenxi and Beiting field headquarters, was encamped at Henei.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，北庭兵馬使王惟良謀作亂，嗣業與裨將荔非元禮討誅之。

translations.literal: On day guisi the Beiting army-and-horse commissioner Wang Weiliang plotted rebellion; Siye with his lieutenant general Lafei Yuanli attacked and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi the Beiting army-and-horse commissioner Wang Weiliang plotted a mutiny; Li Siye and his lieutenant Lafei Yuanli suppressed and killed him.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒之北走也，其平原太守王暕、清河太守宇文寬皆殺其使者來降；

translations.literal: When An Qingxu fled north, his Pingyuan prefect Wang Yan and Qinghe prefect Yuwen Kuan both killed his envoys and came over in surrender;
translations.idiomatic: When An Qingxu fled north, his Pingyuan prefect Wang Yan and Qinghe prefect Yuwen Kuan killed his envoys and surrendered;

sentences.zh: 慶緒使其將蔡希德、安太清攻拔之，生擒以歸，咼於鄴市。

translations.literal: Qingxu sent his generals Cai Xide and An Taiqing to attack and take them, captured them alive and brought them back, and disfigured them in the market at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu sent Cai Xide and An Taiqing to retake the cities, captured them alive, and had their noses cut off in the market at Ye.

sentences.zh: 凡有謀歸者，皆誅及種、族，乃至部曲、州縣、官屬，連坐死者甚眾。

translations.literal: All who plotted to return were put to death extending to seed and clan, even to retainers, prefectures and counties, and subordinate officials; those implicated and executed were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone who plotted to defect was executed together with his clan, retainers, local officials, and subordinates; the dead were innumerable.

sentences.zh: 又與其群臣歃血盟於鄴南，而人心益離。

translations.literal: Again he and his ministers swore a blood oath south of Ye, yet hearts drifted further apart.
translations.idiomatic: He and his ministers swore a blood oath south of Ye, yet loyalty only frayed further.

sentences.zh: 慶緒聞李嗣業在河內，夏，四月，與蔡希德、崔乾祐將步騎二萬，涉沁水攻之，不勝而還。

translations.literal: Qingxu heard that Li Siye was at Henei; in summer, fourth month, with Cai Xide and Cui Qianyou he led twenty thousand foot and horse, crossed the Qin River to attack him, did not prevail, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Li Siye was at Henei, in the fourth month of summer Qingxu led Cai Xide and Cui Qianyou with twenty thousand infantry and cavalry across the Qin River to attack him, failed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，以太子少師虢王巨為河南尹，充東京留守。

translations.literal: On day guimao Prince of Guo Ju, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, was made Henan intendant and charged as Eastern Capital regent.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao Prince of Guo Ju, Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, was appointed Henan intendant and regent of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，新主入太廟。

translations.literal: On day xinmao the new spirit tablets entered the Grand Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao the new spirit tablets were installed in the Grand Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，上享太廟，遂祀昊天上帝；

translations.literal: On day jiayin the emperor offered in the Grand Ancestral Temple, then sacrificed to the Supreme Heavenly Emperor;
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin the emperor offered in the Grand Ancestral Temple, then sacrificed to the Supreme Heavenly Emperor;

sentences.zh: 乙卯，御明鳳門，赦天下。

translations.literal: on day yimao he took the Mingfeng Gate and amnestied the realm.
translations.idiomatic: on yimao he appeared at the Mingfeng Gate and proclaimed a general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 五月，壬午，制停採訪使，改黜陟使為觀察使。

translations.literal: Fifth month, day renwu: by statute the Investigating Commissioners were abolished, and the Promotion-and-Demotion Commissioners were changed to Surveillance Commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, on renwu, the Investigating Commissioners were abolished and the Promotion-and-Demotion Commissioners were renamed Surveillance Commissioners.

sentences.zh: 張鎬性簡澹，不事中要，聞史思明請降，上言：「思明凶險，因亂竊位，力強則眾附，勢奪則人離，彼雖人面，心如野獸，難以德懷，願勿假以威權。

translations.literal: Zhang Gao was by nature simple and detached, did not serve the powerful favorites; hearing that Shi Siming sought surrender, he submitted: "Siming is fierce and treacherous, seized position amid chaos; when his strength is great the multitude attaches, when his momentum is lost men depart—though he has a human face, his heart is like a wild beast; he is hard to win by virtue; I beg that authority and power not be lent him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gao was plain and detached by nature and would not court the powerful. When he heard that Shi Siming was offering to surrender, he memorialized: "Siming is fierce and treacherous; he seized power in the chaos. When he is strong men flock to him; when his power fades they abandon him. Though he wears a human face, his heart is that of a beast. He cannot be won by virtue. Do not grant him authority."

sentences.zh: 」又言：「滑州防禦使許叔冀，狡猾多詐，臨難必變，請征入宿衛。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Xu Shuji, defense commissioner of Huazhou, is crafty and full of deceit; facing peril he is sure to turn—I beg that he be summoned to serve in the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Xu Shuji, defense commissioner of Huazhou, is cunning and treacherous; in a crisis he will surely turn. Summon him to serve in the palace guard."

sentences.zh: 」時上以寵納思明，會中使自范陽及白馬來，皆言思明、叔冀忠懇可信，上以鎬為不切事機，戊子，罷為荊州防禦使；

translations.literal: " At this time the emperor, having favored and accepted Siming, happened to have palace envoys come from Fanyang and Baima, all saying Siming and Shuji were loyal and sincere and could be trusted; the emperor held Gao not attuned to the moment's needs; on day wuzi he was dismissed to be defense commissioner of Jingzhou;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was already inclined to favor Siming. Palace envoys arrived from Fanyang and Baima, all reporting that Siming and Shuji were loyal and trustworthy. The emperor judged Gao out of touch with affairs. On wuzi he was demoted to defense commissioner of Jingzhou;

sentences.zh: 以禮部尚書崔光遠為河南節度使。

translations.literal: Minister of Rites Cui Guangyuan was made Henan military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: and Minister of Rites Cui Guangyuan was appointed Henan military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 張-{后}-生興王佋，才數歲，欲以為嗣。

translations.literal: The Zhang empress had borne Prince of Xing You, only a few years old; the emperor wished to make him heir.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Zhang had borne Prince of Xing Li You, still only a few years old, and the emperor wished to make him heir.

sentences.zh: 上疑未決，從容謂考功郎中、知制誥李揆曰：「成王長，且有功，朕欲立為太子，卿意何如？

translations.literal: The emperor was in doubt and had not decided; at leisure he said to Li Kui, Director of the Bureau of Merit and drafter of edicts: "The Prince of Cheng is eldest and moreover has merit; I wish to establish him as heir apparent—what is your view?
translations.idiomatic: Still undecided, the emperor casually asked Li Kui, Director of the Bureau of Merit and drafter of edicts: "Prince of Cheng is the eldest and has won merit. I wish to make him heir apparent. What do you think?

sentences.zh: 」揆再拜賀曰：「此社稷之福，臣不勝大慶！

translations.literal: " Kui bowed twice in congratulation and said: "This is the altars of state's good fortune; your servant cannot bear such great rejoicing!
translations.idiomatic: Kui bowed twice and exclaimed: "This is the fortune of the state! I cannot contain my joy!"

sentences.zh: 」上喜曰：「朕意決矣。

translations.literal: " The emperor was pleased and said: "My mind is decided.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased. "My mind is made up," he said.

sentences.zh: 」庚寅，立成王俶為皇太子。

translations.literal: " On day gengyin the Prince of Cheng Chu was established as heir apparent.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Prince of Cheng Li Chu was established as heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 揆，玄道之玄孫也。

translations.literal: Kui was the great-great-grandson of Li Xuandao.
translations.idiomatic: Kui was the great-great-grandson of Li Xuandao.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以崔圓為太子少師，李麟為少傅，皆罷政事。

translations.literal: On day yiwei Cui Yuan was made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, Li Lin Junior Mentor—all were removed from governing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei Cui Yuan was made Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent and Li Lin Junior Mentor; both were removed from governing affairs.

sentences.zh: 上頗好鬼神，太常少卿王璵專依鬼神以求媚，每議禮儀，多雜以巫祝俚俗。

translations.literal: The emperor rather favored ghosts and spirits; Wang Yu, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, relied exclusively on ghosts and spirits to seek favor; whenever ritual observances were discussed, he often mixed in shamans, invocations, and vulgar custom.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor favored spirits and omens. Wang Yu, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, courted favor through spirit worship; whenever ritual was discussed, he larded it with shamans, invocations, and vulgar custom.

sentences.zh: 上悅之，以璵為中書侍郎、同平章事。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased with him and made Yu Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow Commissioner with the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and made Yu Vice Director of the Secretariat and Fellow Commissioner with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 贈故常山太守顏杲卿太子太保，謚曰忠節，以其子威明為太僕丞。

translations.literal: The former Changshan prefect Yan Gaoqing was posthumously given Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, posthumous title Loyal and Upright, and his son Weiming was made Assistant Master of the Stud.
translations.idiomatic: The late Changshan prefect Yan Gaoqing was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent with the posthumous title Loyal and Upright, and his son Weiming was appointed Assistant Master of the Stud.

sentences.zh: 杲卿之死也，楊國忠用張通幽之譖，竟無褒贈。

translations.literal: At Gaoqing's death, Yang Guozhong used Zhang Tongyou's slander, and in the end there was no commendation or grant.
translations.idiomatic: At the time of Gaoqing's death, Yang Guozhong had heeded Zhang Tongyou's slander, and no honors were granted.

sentences.zh: 上在鳳翔，顏真卿為御史大夫，泣訴於上。

translations.literal: When the emperor was at Fengxiang, Yan Zhenqing as Censor-in-Chief wept and pleaded before him.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was at Fengxiang, Censor-in-Chief Yan Zhenqing wept as he pleaded his brother's case.

sentences.zh: 上乃出通幽為普安太守，具奏其狀於上皇，上皇杖殺通幽。

translations.literal: The emperor then sent Tongyou out as prefect of Pu'an, fully reported the circumstances to the Retired Emperor, and the Retired Emperor had Tongyou beaten to death with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exiled Tongyou to Pu'an as prefect, reported the full case to the Retired Emperor, and the Retired Emperor had Tongyou beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 杲卿子泉明為王承業所留，因寓居壽陽，為史思明所虜，裹以牛革，送於范陽。

translations.literal: Gaoqing's son Quanming was detained by Wang Chengye and therefore lodged at Shouyang; he was captured by Shi Siming, wrapped in oxhide, and sent to Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing's son Quanming had been detained by Wang Chengye and was living at Shouyang when Shi Siming captured him, bound him in oxhide, and sent him to Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 會安慶緒初立，有赦，得免。

translations.literal: It happened that when An Qingxu had just been established, there was an amnesty, and he was spared.
translations.idiomatic: When An Qingxu first took the throne, a general amnesty spared him.

sentences.zh: 思明降，乃得歸，求其父屍於東京，得之，遂並袁履謙屍棺斂以歸。

translations.literal: When Siming surrendered, he was then able to return; he sought his father's corpse in the Eastern Capital, found it, and together with Yuan Lüqian's corpse placed them in coffins and returned.
translations.idiomatic: After Siming surrendered he was able to return, found his father's body in the Eastern Capital, and brought it home in a coffin together with the remains of Yuan Lüqian.

sentences.zh: 杲卿姊妹女及泉明之子皆流落河北；

translations.literal: Gaoqing's sisters, daughters, and Quanming's sons had all drifted lost in Hebei;
translations.idiomatic: Gaoqing's sisters, daughters, and Quanming's sons had all been scattered across Hebei;

sentences.zh: 真卿時為蒲州刺史，使泉明往求之，泉明號泣求訪，哀感路人，久乃得之。

translations.literal: Zhenqing at the time was prefect of Pu; he sent Quanming to seek them; Quanming wailed and wept in his search, his grief moving passersby on the road, and only after long effort found them.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Zhenqing was then prefect of Pu and sent Quanming to find them. Quanming searched wailing until passersby were moved to tears; only after a long search did he locate them.

sentences.zh: 泉明詣親故乞索，隨所得多少贖之，先姑姊妹而後其子。

translations.literal: Quanming went to kin and old friends to beg and gather; as he obtained more or less he ransomed them, first the paternal aunts and sisters and afterward his own sons.
translations.idiomatic: Quanming begged from kin and friends and ransomed whomever he could, redeeming his aunts and cousins before his own sons.

sentences.zh: 姑女為賊所掠，泉明錢二百緡，欲贖己女，閔其姑愁悴，先贖姑女；

translations.literal: A paternal aunt's daughter had been seized by rebels; Quanming had two hundred strings of cash and wished to ransom his own daughter, but pitying his aunt's haggard grief, he first ransomed the aunt's daughter;
translations.idiomatic: When an aunt's daughter had been seized by rebels, Quanming had two hundred strings of cash and meant to ransom his own daughter, but seeing his aunt's grief, he redeemed her daughter first;

sentences.zh: 比更得錢，求其女，已失所在。

translations.literal: by the time he obtained more cash and sought his daughter, she had already been lost—no knowing where.
translations.idiomatic: by the time he raised more money to ransom his own daughter, she had vanished.

sentences.zh: 遇群從姊妹及父時將吏袁履謙等妻子流落者，皆與之歸，凡五十餘家，三百餘口，均減資糧，一如親戚。

translations.literal: He encountered collateral cousins and sisters and the wives and children of his father's former officers such as Yuan Lüqian who had drifted lost—all were brought back with him; in all more than fifty households, more than three hundred mouths; he equally reduced his provisions and grain, treating them just like kin.
translations.idiomatic: He found cousins and the wives and children of his father's officers, including Yuan Lüqian's family, and brought them all home—more than fifty households, over three hundred people—sharing his provisions with them as though they were kin.

sentences.zh: 至蒲州，直卿悉加贍給，久之，隨其所適而資送之。

translations.literal: When they reached Puzhou, Zhenqing entirely added support and provision; after long time, according to where each was bound he supplied and sent them on.
translations.idiomatic: When they reached Pu, Yan Zhenqing supported them all generously and, in time, furnished each household for the journey to its destination.

sentences.zh: 袁履謙妻疑履謙衣衾儉薄，發棺視之，與杲卿無異，乃始慚服。

translations.literal: Yuan Lüqian's wife suspected Lüqian's burial garments and coverlets were meager; she opened the coffin to look, and they were no different from Gaoqing's—only then did she begin to feel ashamed and submit.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Lüqian's wife suspected that her husband had been buried shabbily; she opened the coffin and found his shroud no less fine than Gaoqing's, and was ashamed.

sentences.zh: 六月，己酉，立太一壇於南郊之東，從王璵之請也。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day jiyou: the Grand Unity altar was established east of the southern suburban altar, following Wang Yu's request.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month, on jiyou, the Grand Unity altar was established east of the southern suburban altar at Wang Yu's request.

sentences.zh: 上嘗不豫，卜雲山川為祟，璵請遣中使與女巫乘驛分禱天下名山大川。

translations.literal: The emperor once was unwell; divination said mountains and rivers were afflicting him; Yu requested dispatching palace envoys and shamans to ride post relays and pray separately at famous mountains and great rivers throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor fell ill, diviners blamed mountain and river spirits. Yu asked that palace envoys and shamans be sent by post relay to pray at famous mountains and rivers across the realm.

sentences.zh: 巫恃勢，所過煩擾州縣，干求受贓。

translations.literal: The shamans relied on their power; wherever they passed they harassed prefectures and counties, importuning and accepting bribes.
translations.idiomatic: The shamans abused their authority, harassing every prefecture and county they passed and extorting bribes.

sentences.zh: 黃州有巫，盛年美色，從無賴少年數十，為蠹尤甚，至黃州，宿於驛捨。

translations.literal: At Huangzhou there was a shaman in the prime of youth and beautiful in appearance, followed by several tens of worthless young men; as a pest she was especially severe; arriving at Huangzhou, she lodged at the post station.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangzhou one shaman, young and beautiful, traveled with several dozen ruffians and preyed on the region worse than most; when she reached Huangzhou she lodged at the post station.

sentences.zh: 刺史左震晨至驛，門扃鎖，不可啟，震怒，破鎖而入，曳巫於階下斬之，所從少年悉斃之，籍其贓數十萬，具以狀聞，且請以其贓代貧民租，遣中使還京師，上無以罪也。

translations.literal: Prefect Zuo Zhen came early to the station; the gate was barred and locked and could not be opened; Zhen was enraged, broke the lock and entered, dragged the shaman to the steps below and beheaded her, executed all the young men who followed, registered their illicit gains in the hundreds of thousands, fully reported the circumstances, and moreover requested using their gains in place of poor commoners' land tax; he sent the palace envoy back to the capital—the emperor had no means to punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Zuo Zhen came to the station at dawn and found the gate barred. Enraged, he broke in, dragged the shaman to the steps and beheaded her, executed all her followers, seized hundreds of thousands in stolen goods, reported the case in full, and asked to apply the confiscated wealth to poor taxpayers' land dues. He sent the palace envoy back to the capital; the emperor could not punish him.

sentences.zh: 以開府儀同三司李嗣業為懷州刺史，充鎮西、北庭行營節度使。

translations.literal: Li Siye, Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Pouch, was made prefect of Huaizhou and commissioned as Zhenxi and Beiting field headquarters military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siye, Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Pouch, was appointed prefect of Huaizhou and military commissioner of the Zhenxi and Beiting field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 山人韓穎改造新歷，丁巳，初行穎歷。

translations.literal: The mountain recluse Han Ying reformed and made a new calendar; on day dingsi the Ying calendar was first put into practice.
translations.idiomatic: The recluse Han Ying devised a new calendar; on dingsi the Ying calendar was first adopted.

sentences.zh: 戊午，敕兩京陷賊官，三司推究未畢者皆釋之；

translations.literal: On day wuwu, an edict was issued regarding officials of the Two Capitals who had fallen to the rebels: all those whose cases the Three Departments had not yet finished investigating were released;
translations.idiomatic: On the wuwu day, the emperor decreed that officials of the Two Capitals who had served under the rebels and whose cases the Three Departments had not yet completed would be released;

sentences.zh: 已貶、降者續處分。

translations.literal: Those already demoted or reduced in rank were to receive further disposition.
translations.idiomatic: Those already demoted or degraded would continue to be dealt with separately.

sentences.zh: 太子少師房琯既失職，頗怏怏，多稱疾不朝，而賓客朝夕盈門，其黨為之揚言於朝云：「琯有文武才，宜大用。

translations.literal: Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Fang Guan, having lost his post, was quite resentful and often claimed illness and did not attend court, yet guests morning and evening filled his gate; his faction spread word at court, saying, "Guan has civil and military talent and ought to be greatly employed."
translations.idiomatic: Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent Fang Guan, stripped of office, brooded over his fall and often pleaded illness to stay away from court, while retainers crowded his gate from dawn till dusk. His clique peddled a story at court: "Guan has both civil and military gifts and deserves a greater post."

sentences.zh: 」上聞而惡之，下制數琯罪，貶幽州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and detested this; he issued an edict enumerating Guan's offenses and demoted him to prefect of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of it he was revolted. He issued an edict listing Guan's offenses and banished him to be prefect of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 前祭酒劉秩貶閬州刺史，京兆尹嚴武貶巴州刺史；

translations.literal: The former Libationer Liu Zhi was demoted to prefect of Langzhou, and the Metropolitan Governor Yan Wu was demoted to prefect of Bazhou;
translations.idiomatic: Former Imperial University Libationer Liu Zhi was demoted to prefect of Langzhou, and Metropolitan Governor Yan Wu to prefect of Bazhou;

sentences.zh: 皆琯黨也。

translations.literal: all were Guan's faction.
translations.idiomatic: All were members of Guan's faction.

sentences.zh: 初，史思明以列將事來盧軍使烏知義，知義善待之。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shi Siming had served as a subordinate general under Youzhou military commissioner Wu Zhiyi; Zhiyi treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Shi Siming had served under Youzhou military commissioner Wu Zhiyi as a line officer, and Zhiyi treated him kindly.

sentences.zh: 知義子承恩為信都太守，以郡降思明，思明思舊恩而全之。

translations.literal: Zhiyi's son Cheng'en was prefect of Xingdu; he surrendered the commandery to Siming, and Siming, mindful of old kindness, spared him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyi's son Cheng'en was prefect of Xingdu and surrendered the commandery to Siming, who, remembering old favors, spared him.

sentences.zh: 及安慶緒敗，承恩說思明降唐。

translations.literal: When An Qingxu was defeated, Cheng'en urged Siming to submit to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When An Qingxu was defeated, Cheng'en urged Siming to submit to Tang.

sentences.zh: 李光弼以思明終當叛亂，而承恩為思明所親信，陰使圖之；

translations.literal: Li Guangbi believed Siming would eventually rebel again; since Cheng'en was trusted by Siming, he secretly had him plot against him;
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi was sure Siming would rebel again. Because Cheng'en enjoyed Siming's trust, Guangbi secretly set him to plotting against his master;

sentences.zh: 又勸上以承恩為范陽節度副使，賜阿史那承慶鐵券，令共圖思明，上從之。

translations.literal: he also urged the emperor to appoint Cheng'en military vice commissioner of Fanyang, grant Ashina Chengqing an iron certificate, and have them jointly plot against Siming; the emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: he also persuaded the emperor to name Cheng'en vice commissioner of Fanyang, grant Ashina Chengqing an iron certificate of mercy, and have the two of them plot against Siming together. The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 承恩多以私財募部曲，又數衣婦人服詣諸將營說誘之，諸將以白思明，思明疑未察。

translations.literal: Cheng'en often used personal wealth to recruit retainers, and repeatedly donned women's dress to visit the generals' camps to persuade and entice them; the generals reported this to Siming, but Siming suspected yet had not perceived clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng'en spent his own money to raise private troops and repeatedly went about the generals' camps in women's dress to win them over. The generals reported this to Siming, who grew suspicious but had not yet uncovered the plot.

sentences.zh: 會承恩入京師，上使內侍李思敬與之俱至范陽宣慰。

translations.literal: When Cheng'en entered the capital, the emperor sent the palace attendant Li Sijing to accompany him to Fanyang to proclaim consolation.
translations.idiomatic: When Cheng'en came to the capital, the emperor sent the palace attendant Li Sijing to accompany him to Fanyang on a mission of consolation.

sentences.zh: 承恩既宣旨，思明留承恩館於府中，帷其床，伏二人於床下。

translations.literal: After Cheng'en had proclaimed the imperial message, Siming lodged him in the mansion, curtained his bed, and hid two men beneath the bed.
translations.idiomatic: After Cheng'en had delivered the imperial message, Siming lodged him in his mansion, hung curtains around his bed, and hid two men beneath it.

sentences.zh: 承恩少子在范陽，思明使省其父。

translations.literal: Cheng'en's youngest son was in Fanyang; Siming had him visit his father.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng'en's youngest son was in Fanyang; Siming sent him to visit his father.

sentences.zh: 夜中，承恩密謂其子曰：「吾受命除此逆胡，當以吾為節度使。

translations.literal: In the night Cheng'en secretly told his son, "I have received orders to remove this rebellious barbarian; they are to make me military commissioner."
translations.idiomatic: In the night Cheng'en whispered to his son, "I have orders to remove this rebel chieftain—they mean to make me military commissioner."

sentences.zh: 」二人於床下大呼而出。

translations.literal: The two men beneath the bed shouted and burst out.
translations.idiomatic: The two men under the bed shouted and leaped out.

sentences.zh: 思明乃執承恩，索其裝囊，得鐵券及光弼牒，牒云：「承慶事成則付鐵券；

translations.literal: Siming then seized Cheng'en and searched his baggage, finding the iron certificate and Guangbi's dispatch; the dispatch read, "If Chengqing's affair succeeds, then deliver the iron certificate;
translations.idiomatic: Siming then seized Cheng'en and searched his baggage, finding the iron certificate and a dispatch from Guangbi that read, "If Chengqing's affair succeeds, deliver the iron certificate;

sentences.zh: 不然，不可付也。

translations.literal: otherwise, it must not be delivered."
translations.idiomatic: otherwise, do not deliver it."

sentences.zh: 」又得簿書數百紙，皆先從思明反者將士名。

translations.literal: He also found several hundred sheets of registers, all listing officers and men who had first followed Siming in rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: He also found several hundred pages of registers listing every officer and soldier who had first followed him in rebellion.

sentences.zh: 思明責之曰：「我何負於汝而為此！

translations.literal: Siming reproached him, "What have I failed to do for you, that you do this!"
translations.idiomatic: Siming rebuked him: "What wrong have I done you, that you would do this!"

sentences.zh: 」承恩謝曰：「死罪，此皆李光弼之謀也。

translations.literal: Cheng'en apologized, "Capital crime—this is entirely Li Guangbi's plot."
translations.idiomatic: Cheng'en pleaded, "A capital offense—but this was all Li Guangbi's doing."

sentences.zh: 」思明乃集將佐吏民，西向大哭曰：「臣以十三萬眾降朝廷，何負陛下，而欲殺臣！

translations.literal: Siming then assembled officers, clerks, and commoners, faced west, and wept loudly, "Your servant led one hundred thirty thousand men in surrender to the court—how have I failed Your Majesty, that you wish to kill me!"
translations.idiomatic: Siming then gathered his officers, clerks, and townspeople, faced west, and wailed, "I surrendered one hundred thirty thousand men to the court—how have I wronged Your Majesty, that you would seek my life!"

sentences.zh: 」遂榜殺承恩父子，連坐死者二百餘人。

translations.literal: He then had Cheng'en and his son executed by public notice; more than two hundred died by association.
translations.idiomatic: He then had Cheng'en and his son executed by posted proclamation; more than two hundred others died by association.

sentences.zh: 承恩弟承玼免。

translations.literal: Cheng'en's younger brother Chengbi was spared.
translations.idiomatic: Cheng'en's younger brother Chengbi was spared.

sentences.zh: 思明囚思敬，表上其狀。

translations.literal: Siming imprisoned Sijing and memorialized the full account.
translations.idiomatic: Siming imprisoned Sijing and sent a memorial reporting the whole affair.

sentences.zh: 上遣中使慰諭思明曰：「此非朝廷與光弼之意，皆承恩所為，殺之甚善。

translations.literal: The emperor sent a palace envoy to console Siming, saying, "This was not the intent of the court or Guangbi—it was all Cheng'en's doing; killing him was altogether right."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy to reassure Siming: "This was not the court's intent, nor Guangbi's—it was all Cheng'en's doing. You were right to kill him."

sentences.zh: 會三司議陷賊官罪狀至范陽，思明謂諸將曰：「陳希烈輩皆朝廷大臣，上皇自棄之幸蜀，今猶不免於死，況吾屬本從安祿山反乎！

translations.literal: When the Three Departments' deliberations on the crimes of officials who had fallen to the rebels reached Fanyang, Siming said to the generals, "Chen Xilie and the like were all great ministers of the court; the Retired Emperor himself abandoned them and went to Shu, yet they still do not escape death—how much more we, who originally followed An Lushan in rebellion!"
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Departments' findings on officials who had served the rebels reached Fanyang, Siming told his generals, "Men like Chen Xilie were great ministers of the court. The Retired Emperor himself cast them off and fled to Shu, yet they still could not escape death—how much less can we, who rose with An Lushan!"

sentences.zh: 」諸將請思明表求誅光弼，思明從之，命判官耿仁智與其僚張不矜為表云：「陛下不為臣誅光弼，臣當自引兵就太原誅之。

translations.literal: The generals asked Siming to memorialize requesting execution of Guangbi; Siming agreed and ordered his aide Geng Renzhi and his colleague Zhang Bujin to draft a memorial saying, "If Your Majesty will not execute Guangbi for your servant, your servant will himself lead troops to Taiyuan and execute him."
translations.idiomatic: The generals urged Siming to memorialize demanding Guangbi's death. Siming agreed and told his aide Geng Renzhi and colleague Zhang Bujin to draft a memorial: "If Your Majesty will not kill Guangbi for me, I shall lead my own troops to Taiyuan and kill him myself."

sentences.zh: 」不矜草表以示思明，及將入函，仁智悉削去之。

translations.literal: Bujin drafted the memorial and showed it to Siming; when it was about to be placed in the envelope, Renzhi cut it all away.
translations.idiomatic: Bujin drafted the memorial and showed it to Siming; as it was about to be sealed, Renzhi cut away every word.

sentences.zh: 寫表者以白思明，思明命執二人斬之。

translations.literal: The copyist reported this to Siming; Siming ordered the two seized and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The copyist reported it to Siming, who ordered both men seized and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 仁智事思明久，思明憐，欲活之，復召入，謂曰：「我任使汝垂三十年，今日非我負汝。

translations.literal: Renzhi had served Siming long; Siming pitied him and wished to spare him, and summoned him in again, saying, "I have employed you for nearly thirty years—today it is not I who have failed you."
translations.idiomatic: Renzhi had served Siming for many years; Siming took pity and meant to spare him, and called him back in, saying, "I have employed you for nearly thirty years—today it is not I who have failed you."

sentences.zh: 」仁智大呼曰：「人生會有一死，得盡忠義，死之善者也。

translations.literal: Renzhi cried out, "Every human life must end once; to fulfill loyalty and righteousness—that is the good death."
translations.idiomatic: Renzhi shouted, "Every man must die once—to die having fulfilled loyalty and righteousness is the good death."

sentences.zh: 今從大夫反，不過延歲月，豈若速死之愈乎！

translations.literal: To follow you, Lord, in rebellion gains no more than a few extra months—how is that better than dying quickly!"
translations.idiomatic: To follow you in rebellion buys no more than a few extra months—how is that better than dying now!"

sentences.zh: 」思明怒，亂捶之，腦流於地。

translations.literal: Siming was enraged and beat him wildly; his brains streamed onto the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Siming flew into a rage and beat him until his brains ran on the ground.

sentences.zh: 烏承玼太原，李光弼表為昌化郡王，充石嶺軍使。

translations.literal: Wu Chengbi submitted Taiyuan; Li Guangbi memorialized creating him Prince of Changhua and appointing him Shiling army commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chengbi surrendered Taiyuan; Li Guangbi memorialized to create him Prince of Changhua and appoint him Shiling army commissioner.

sentences.zh: 秋，七月，丙戌，初鑄當十大錢，文曰「乾元重寶」，從御史中丞第五琦之謀也。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on day bingxu, the government first cast ten-to-one heavy coins inscribed "Qianyuan Heavy Treasure," following the plan of Vice Censor-in-Chief Diwu Qi.
translations.idiomatic: In autumn, the seventh month, on the bingxu day, the government first cast ten-cash heavy coins inscribed "Qianyuan Heavy Treasure," following the plan of Vice Censor-in-Chief Diwu Qi.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，冊命回紇可汗曰英武威遠毘伽闕可汗，以上幼女寧國公主妻之。

translations.literal: On dinghai, the Uyghur qaghan was enfeoffed with the title Yingwu Weiyuan Pijia Que Qaghan, and the emperor's youngest daughter, Princess Ningguo, was given to him in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai the Uyghur qaghan was enfeoffed as Yingwu Weiyuan Pijia Que Qaghan, and the emperor gave him his youngest daughter, Princess Ningguo, in marriage.

sentences.zh: 以監漢中王瑀為冊禮使，右司郎中李巽副之；

translations.literal: Prince of Hanzhong Wang Yu, Director of the Palace Domestic Service, was made chief envoy for the enfeoffment; Vice Director of the Right Secretariat Li Xun served as his deputy;
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Hanzhong Wang Yu, Director of the Palace Domestic Service, was made chief enfeoffment envoy, with Vice Director of the Right Secretariat Li Xun as his deputy;

sentences.zh: 命左僕射裴冕送公主至境上。

translations.literal: Left Vice Minister of State Pei Mian was ordered to escort the princess to the border.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Minister of State Pei Mian was ordered to escort the princess to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 戊子，又以司勳員餐郎鮮於叔明為瑀副。

translations.literal: On wuzi, Xianyu Shuming, extrabureau director in the Bureau of Merit, was also made Wang Yu's deputy.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Xianyu Shuming of the Bureau of Merit was also appointed Wang Yu's deputy.

sentences.zh: 叔明，仲通之弟也。

translations.literal: Shuming was the younger brother of Zhongtong.
translations.idiomatic: Shuming was the younger brother of Zhongtong.

sentences.zh: 甲子，上送寧國公主至咸陽，公主辭訣曰：「國家事重，死且無恨！

translations.literal: On jiazi, the emperor escorted Princess Ningguo to Xianyang; the princess took leave saying, "The affairs of the state weigh heavily—I can die without regret!"
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi the emperor escorted Princess Ningguo as far as Xianyang. Taking her leave, the princess said, "The state comes first—even death would hold no regret for me!"

sentences.zh: 」上流涕而還。

translations.literal: The emperor wept and returned.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and turned back.

sentences.zh: 瑀等至回紇牙帳，可汗衣赭袍胡帽，坐帳中榻上，儀衛甚盛，引瑀等立於帳外，瑀不拜而立，可汗曰：「我與天可汗兩國之君，君臣有禮，何得不拜！

translations.literal: Yu and the rest reached the Uyghur royal camp. The qaghan wore a russet robe and Turkic cap and sat on a couch within the tent; his guard was very imposing. He had Yu and the others stand outside the tent. Yu did not bow but stood upright. The qaghan said, "I and the Heavenly Qaghan are sovereigns of two states—between minister and lord there is propriety; how can you not bow!"
translations.idiomatic: When Yu and his party reached the Uyghur royal camp, the qaghan wore a russet robe and Turkic cap and sat on a couch inside the tent, his escort magnificent in array. He had Yu and the others stand outside the tent. Yu stood without bowing. The qaghan said, "I and the Heavenly Qaghan are sovereigns of two realms—between lord and minister there is ritual propriety. How can you not bow!"

sentences.zh: 」瑀與叔明對曰：「向者唐與諸國為婚，皆以宗室女為公主。

translations.literal: Yu and Shuming replied together, "Formerly, when Tang allied in marriage with the various states, each took an imperial clanswoman as princess."
translations.idiomatic: Yu and Shuming answered together, "In former times, when Tang allied in marriage with foreign states, it always sent clanswomen as princesses."

sentences.zh: 今天子以可汗有功，自以所生女妻可汗。

translations.literal: Today the Son of Heaven, because the qaghan has merit, has himself given his own daughter born in the purple to be the qaghan's wife.
translations.idiomatic: Today the Son of Heaven, because the qaghan has rendered great service, has given his own daughter born in the purple to be the qaghan's wife.

sentences.zh: 恩禮至重，可汗奈何以子婿傲婦翁，坐榻上受冊命邪！

translations.literal: The grace and ritual are supremely weighty—how can the qaghan, as son-in-law, show arrogance toward his wife's father and sit on a couch to receive the enfeoffment edict!"
translations.idiomatic: The favor and ceremony are of the utmost weight—how can the qaghan, as son-in-law, show arrogance toward his wife's father and sit on a couch to receive the enfeoffment!"

sentences.zh: 」可汗改容，起受冊命。

translations.literal: The qaghan changed his expression, rose, and received the enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: The qaghan changed countenance, rose, and received the enfeoffment standing.

sentences.zh: 明日，立公主為可敦，舉國皆喜。

translations.literal: The next day the princess was installed as khatun, and the whole nation rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the princess was installed as khatun, and the whole nation rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 乙未，郭子儀入朝。

translations.literal: On yiwei, Guo Ziyi entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, Guo Ziyi came to court.

sentences.zh: 八月，壬寅，以青、登等五州節度使許叔冀為滑、濮等六州節度使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day renyin, Xu Shuji, military commissioner of Qing, Deng, and five other prefectures, was made military commissioner of Hua, Pu, and six other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, on the renyin day, Xu Shuji, military commissioner of Qing, Deng, and five other prefectures, was transferred to be military commissioner of Hua, Pu, and six other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，李光弼入朝。

translations.literal: On gengxu, Li Guangbi entered court.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, Li Guangbi came to court.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，以郭子儀為中書令，光弼為侍中。

translations.literal: On bingchen, Guo Ziyi was made Director of the Department of State Affairs and Guangbi Attendant-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: On bingchen, Guo Ziyi was made Director of the Department of State Affairs and Li Guangbi Attendant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 丁巳，子儀詣行營。

translations.literal: On dingsi, Ziyi went to the field headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi, Ziyi returned to the field headquarters.

sentences.zh: 回紇遣其臣骨啜特勒及帝德將驍騎三千助討安慶緒，上命朔方左武鋒使僕固懷恩領之。

translations.literal: The Uyghurs sent their ministers Guchuo Teli and Dide to lead three thousand crack horsemen to help attack An Qingxu; the emperor ordered Pugu Huai'en of the Shuofang Left Martial Vanguard to command them.
translations.idiomatic: The Uyghurs sent their ministers Guchuo Teli and Dide with three thousand crack horsemen to help attack An Qingxu; the emperor ordered Pugu Huai'en of the Shuofang Left Martial Vanguard to lead them.

sentences.zh: 九月，庚午朔，以右羽林大將軍趙泚為蒲、同、虢三州節度使。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, the first day of the month gengwu, Right General of the Feathered Forest Zhao Ci was made military commissioner of the three prefectures Pu, Tong, and Guo.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, on the first day gengwu, Right General of the Feathered Forest Zhao Ci was made military commissioner of Pu, Tong, and Guo.

sentences.zh: 丙子，招討党項使王仲升斬党項酋長拓跋戎德，傳首。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Wang Zhongsheng, commissioner for suppressing the Qiang tribes, beheaded the Qiang chief Tuoba Rongde and sent his head.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, Wang Zhongsheng, commissioner for suppressing the Qiang tribes, beheaded the Qiang chief Tuoba Rongde and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 安慶緒之初至鄴也，雖枝黨離析，猶據七郡六十餘城，甲兵資糧豐備。

translations.literal: When An Qingxu first reached Ye, though his branch supporters had scattered, he still held more than sixty cities in seven commanderies, with armor, weapons, provisions, and grain abundantly supplied.
translations.idiomatic: When An Qingxu first reached Ye, though his faction had splintered, he still held more than sixty cities across seven commanderies, with armor, weapons, and provisions in abundance.

sentences.zh: 慶緒不親政事，專以繕台沼樓船、酣飲為事。

translations.literal: Qingxu did not attend to government affairs himself, devoting himself entirely to repairing terraces, ponds, and tower-ships and to heavy drinking.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu paid no attention to government, devoting himself to building terraces, ponds, and tower-ships and to heavy drinking.

sentences.zh: 其大臣高尚、張通儒等爭權不葉，無復綱紀。

translations.literal: His great ministers Gao Shang, Zhang Tongru, and others struggled for power without agreement; order was gone.
translations.idiomatic: His chief ministers Gao Shang, Zhang Tongru, and others fought for power without reconciling, and discipline collapsed.

sentences.zh: 蔡希德有才略，部兵精銳，而性剛，好直言，通儒譖而殺之；

translations.literal: Cai Xide had stratagem and talent and his troops were elite and sharp, but he was stubborn by nature and fond of blunt speech; Tongru slandered him and had him killed;
translations.idiomatic: Cai Xide was capable and his troops were elite, but he was stubborn and spoke bluntly; Tongru slandered him and had him killed;

sentences.zh: 麾下數千人皆逃散，諸將怨怒不為用。

translations.literal: Several thousand under his command all fled and scattered; the generals were resentful and angry and would not serve.
translations.idiomatic: Several thousand of his men fled and scattered, and the generals, resentful and angry, refused to fight.

sentences.zh: 以崔乾祐為天下兵馬使，總中外兵，乾祐愎戾好殺，士卒不附。

translations.literal: Cui Qianyou was made commissioner of all armies under heaven, commanding internal and external forces; Qianyou was obstinate, harsh, and fond of killing, and the soldiers would not attach to him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Qianyou was made commissioner of all armies under heaven, commanding forces within and without; Qianyou was obstinate and bloodthirsty, and the soldiers would not follow him.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，命朔方郭子儀、淮西魯炅、興平李奐、滑濮許叔冀、鎮西、北庭李嗣業、鄭蔡季廣琛、河南崔光遠七節度使及平盧兵馬使董秦將步騎二十萬討慶緒；

translations.literal: On gengyin, Guo Ziyi of Shuofang, Lu Huang of Huaixi, Li Huan of Xingping, Xu Shuji of Hua-Pu, Li Siye of Zhenxi and Beiting, Ji Guangchen of Zheng-Cai, and Cui Guangyuan of Henan—seven military commissioners—and Dong Qin, infantry-cavalry commissioner of Pinglu, were ordered to lead two hundred thousand foot and horse to attack Qingxu;
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, seven military commissioners—Guo Ziyi of Shuofang, Lu Huang of Huaixi, Li Huan of Xingping, Xu Shuji of Hua-Pu, Li Siye of Zhenxi and Beiting, Ji Guangchen of Zheng-Cai, and Cui Guangyuan of Henan—together with Dong Qin, infantry-cavalry commissioner of Pinglu, were ordered to lead two hundred thousand foot and horse against Qingxu;

sentences.zh: 又命河東李光弼、關內、澤潞王思禮二節度使將所部兵助之。

translations.literal: Li Guangbi of Hedong and Wang Sili of Guannei and Zelu—the two commissioners—were also ordered to lead their own troops to assist.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangbi of Hedong and Wang Sili of Guannei and Zelu were also ordered to bring their own troops to reinforce them.

sentences.zh: 上以子儀、光弼皆元勳，難相統屬，故不置元帥，但以宦官開府儀同三司魚朝恩為觀軍容宣慰處置使。

translations.literal: Because Ziyi and Guangbi were both founding merit-holders and hard to place one under the other, the emperor did not appoint a supreme commander but only made the eunuch Yu Chaoen, Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Pouch, Army-Watching Pacification and Disposition Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Because Ziyi and Guangbi were both founding merit-holders and neither could readily command the other, the emperor appointed no supreme commander but only the eunuch Yu Chaoen, Grand Master of the Palace with the Golden Pouch, as Army-Watching Pacification and Disposition Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 觀軍容之名自此始。

translations.literal: The title Army-Watching Commissioner began from this.
translations.idiomatic: The title Army-Watching Commissioner dates from this appointment.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，廣州奏：大食、波斯圍州城，刺史韋利見逾城走，二國兵掠倉庫，焚廬舍，浮海而去。

translations.literal: On guisi, Guangzhou reported: the Arabs and Persians besieged the prefectural city; Prefect Wei Lijian climbed over the wall and fled; the troops of the two states plundered the storehouses, burned houses, and departed by sea.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi, Guangzhou reported that Arab and Persian forces had besieged the prefectural city; Prefect Wei Lijian fled over the wall; the troops of both states plundered the storehouses, burned the buildings, and sailed away by sea.

sentences.zh: 冬，十月，甲辰，冊太子，更名曰豫。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on jiachen, the Heir Apparent was formally installed and his name changed to Yu.
translations.idiomatic: In winter, the tenth month, on jiachen, the Heir Apparent was formally installed and his name changed to Yu.

sentences.zh: 自中興以來，群下無復賜物，至是，始有新鑄大錢，百官、六軍沾賚有差。

translations.literal: Since the restoration, subordinates had again received no gifts of goods; now, with the newly cast heavy coins, the hundred officials and Six Armies received largesse in varying measure.
translations.idiomatic: Since the restoration, officials had received no gifts of goods; now, with the newly cast heavy coins, the hundred officials and the Six Armies received largesse in varying amounts.

sentences.zh: 郭子儀引兵自杏園濟河，東至獲嘉，破安太清，斬首四千級，捕虜五百人。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi led troops across the river from Xingyuan, east to Huojia, defeated An Taiqing, cut off four thousand heads, and captured five hundred prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi led his army across the river from Xingyuan and east to Huojia, where he defeated An Taiqing, took four thousand heads, and captured five hundred prisoners.

sentences.zh: 太清走保衛州，子儀進圍之；

translations.literal: Taiqing fled to hold Weizhou; Ziyi advanced to besiege it;
translations.idiomatic: Taiqing fled into Weizhou; Ziyi advanced to besiege it;

sentences.zh: 丙午，遣使告捷。

translations.literal: On bingwu, he sent an envoy to report victory.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu he sent an envoy to report victory.

sentences.zh: 魯炅自陽武濟，季廣琛、崔光遠自酸棗濟，與李嗣業兵皆會子儀於衛州。

translations.literal: Lu Huang crossed from Yangwu, Ji Guangchen and Cui Guangyuan crossed from Suanzao, and Li Siye's troops all joined Ziyi at Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huang crossed from Yangwu, Ji Guangchen and Cui Guangyuan from Suanzao, and Li Siye's troops all joined Ziyi at Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 慶緒悉舉鄴中之眾七萬救衛州，分三軍，以崔乾祐將上軍，田承嗣將下軍，慶緒自將中軍。
