translations.literal: Qingxu mustered all seventy thousand men in Ye to rescue Weizhou, dividing into three armies: Cui Qianyou led the upper army, Tian Chengsi the lower, and Qingxu himself the center.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu mustered all seventy thousand men in Ye to relieve Weizhou, dividing them into three armies: Cui Qianyou commanded the upper army, Tian Chengsi the lower, and Qingxu himself the center.

sentences.zh: 子儀使善射者三千人伏於壘垣之內，令曰：「我退，賊必逐我，汝乃登壘，鼓噪而射之。

translations.literal: Ziyi placed three thousand skilled archers hidden within the ramparts, ordering: "When I retreat, the rebels will surely pursue; you then mount the ramparts, raise a clamor, and shoot."
translations.idiomatic: Ziyi hid three thousand skilled archers inside the ramparts with orders: "When I fall back, the rebels will pursue—then mount the walls, raise a clamor, and shoot."

sentences.zh: 」既而與慶緒戰，偽退，賊逐之，至壘下，伏兵起射之，矢如雨注，賊還走，子儀復引兵逐之，慶緒大敗。

translations.literal: They then fought Qingxu, feigned retreat, and the rebels pursued; at the foot of the ramparts the ambush rose and shot; arrows fell like rain; the rebels turned and fled, and Ziyi again led troops in pursuit; Qingxu was badly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They then fought Qingxu, feigned a retreat, and the rebels pursued. At the foot of the ramparts the ambush rose and shot; arrows fell like rain. The rebels turned and fled, and Ziyi pursued again. Qingxu was routed.

sentences.zh: 獲其弟慶和，殺之。

translations.literal: His brother Qinghe was captured and killed.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Qinghe was captured and executed.

sentences.zh: 遂拔衛州。

translations.literal: Weizhou was then taken.
translations.idiomatic: Weizhou was then taken.

sentences.zh: 慶緒走，子儀等追之至鄴，許叔冀、董秦、王思禮及河東兵馬使薛兼訓皆引兵繼至。

translations.literal: Qingxu fled; Ziyi and the rest pursued to Ye; Xu Shuji, Dong Qin, Wang Sili, and Hedong infantry-cavalry commissioner Xue Jianxun all led troops in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu fled; Ziyi and the others pursued to Ye; Xu Shuji, Dong Qin, Wang Sili, and Hedong infantry-cavalry commissioner Xue Jianxun all brought their armies up in turn.

sentences.zh: 慶緒收餘眾拒戰於愁思岡，又敗。

translations.literal: Qingxu gathered the remnant force and resisted at Chousi Ridge, and was again defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu gathered his remnant force and made a stand at Chousi Ridge, but was defeated again.

sentences.zh: 前後斬首三萬級，捕虜千人。

translations.literal: In all, thirty thousand heads were cut off before and after, and one thousand captives taken.
translations.idiomatic: In all, thirty thousand heads were taken and one thousand prisoners captured.

sentences.zh: 慶緒乃入城固守，子儀等圍之，李光弼引兵繼至。

translations.literal: Qingxu then entered the city and held firm; Ziyi and the rest besieged it, and Li Guangbi led troops to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Qingxu then shut himself in the city; Ziyi and the others besieged it, and Li Guangbi brought his army up behind them.

sentences.zh: 慶緒窘急，遣薛嵩求救於史思明，且請以位讓之。

translations.literal: Qingxu, hard pressed, sent Xue Song to beg Shi Siming for rescue and offered to yield his position to him.
translations.idiomatic: Hard pressed, Qingxu sent Xue Song to beg Shi Siming for rescue and offered to yield his throne to him.

sentences.zh: 思明發范陽兵十三萬欲救鄴，觀望未敢進，先遣李歸仁將步騎一萬軍於滏陽，遙為慶緒聲勢。

translations.literal: Siming raised one hundred thirty thousand troops from Fanyang intending to rescue Ye but watched and dared not advance; he first sent Li Guiren with ten thousand foot and horse to encamp at Fuyang, lending distant force to Qingxu's situation.
translations.idiomatic: Siming raised one hundred thirty thousand troops from Fanyang to rescue Ye but held back, daring not advance. He first sent Li Guiren with ten thousand foot and horse to camp at Fuyang, lending distant support to Qingxu's cause.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，上皇幸化清宮；

translations.literal: On jiayin, the Retired Emperor visited the Huaqing Palace;
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, Retired Emperor Xuanzong visited the Huaqing Palace;

sentences.zh: 十一月，丁丑，還京師。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on dingchou, he returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on dingchou, he returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 崔光遠拔魏州；

translations.literal: Cui Guangyuan took Weizhou;
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guangyuan captured Weizhou;

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以前兵部侍郎蕭華為魏州防禦使。

translations.literal: On bingxu, former Vice Minister of War Xiao Hua was made defense commissioner of Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu, former Vice Minister of War Xiao Hua was appointed defense commissioner of Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 會史思明分軍為三，一出邢、洛，一出冀、貝，一自洹水趣魏州。

translations.literal: When Shi Siming divided his army into three—one out through Xing and Luo, one through Ji and Bei, and one from the Huan River toward Weizhou—
translations.idiomatic: When Shi Siming divided his army into three—one column through Xing and Luo, one through Ji and Bei, and one from the Huan River toward Weizhou—

sentences.zh: 郭子儀奏以崔光遠代華，十二月，癸卯，敕以光遠領魏州刺史。

translations.literal: Guo Ziyi memorialized to have Cui Guangyuan replace Hua; in the twelfth month, on guimao, an edict made Guangyuan prefect of Weizhou in addition.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Ziyi memorialized to replace Hua with Cui Guangyuan; in the twelfth month, on guimao, an edict appointed Guangyuan prefect of Weizhou as well.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，置浙江西道節度使，領蘇、潤等十州，以升州刺史韋黃裳為之。

translations.literal: On jiachen, the Zhejiang West Circuit military commissioner was established, governing Su, Run, and ten other prefectures; Shengzhou Prefect Wei Huangshang was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen, the Zhejiang West Circuit military commissioner was established over Su, Run, and ten other prefectures; Shengzhou Prefect Wei Huangshang was appointed to the post.

sentences.zh: 庚戌，置浙江東道節度使，領越、睦等八州，以戶部尚書李峘為之，兼淮南節度使。

translations.literal: On gengxu, the Zhejiang East Circuit military commissioner was established, governing Yue, Mu, and eight other prefectures; Minister of Revenue Li Xian was appointed, also holding the Huainan commission.
translations.idiomatic: On gengxu, the Zhejiang East Circuit military commissioner was established over Yue, Mu, and eight other prefectures; Minister of Revenue Li Xian was appointed, with the Huainan commission added.

sentences.zh: 己未，群臣請上尊號曰乾元大聖光天文武孝感皇帝；

translations.literal: On jiwei, the hundred officials requested for the emperor the honorific title Emperor of Great Sagely Brilliance, Civil and Martial Filial Piety of the Qianyuan era;
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei, the officials petitioned that the emperor take the honorific title Emperor of Great Sagely Brilliance, Civil and Martial Filial Piety of the Qianyuan era;

sentences.zh: 許之。

translations.literal: He assented.
translations.idiomatic: He assented.

sentences.zh: 史思明乘崔光遠初至，引兵大下，光遠使將軍李處崟拒之。

translations.literal: Shi Siming, while Guangyuan had only just arrived, led a great descent of troops; Guangyuan sent General Li Chuyin to resist.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Siming, while Guangyuan had only just arrived, launched a major offensive; Guangyuan sent General Li Chuyin to resist.

sentences.zh: 賊勢盛，處崟連戰不利，還趣城。

translations.literal: The rebel strength was great; Chuyin fought repeatedly without success and turned back toward the city.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel force was overwhelming; Chuyin fought several engagements without success and fell back toward the city.

sentences.zh: 賊追至城下，揚言曰：「處崟召我來，何為不出！

translations.literal: The rebels pursued to beneath the walls and shouted, "Chuyin summoned us—why do you not come out!"
translations.idiomatic: The rebels pursued to the foot of the walls and shouted, "Chuyin invited us here—why won't you come out!"

sentences.zh: 」光遠信之，腰斬處崟。

translations.literal: " Guangyuan believed it, and had Chuyin cut down at the waist.
translations.idiomatic: Guangyuan believed them and had Li Chuyin executed by severing him at the waist.

sentences.zh: 處崟，驍將，眾所恃也，既死，眾無鬥志，光遠脫身走還汴州。

translations.literal: Chuyin was a fierce general on whom the masses relied; once he was dead the masses had no fighting will, and Guangyuan slipped away and fled back to Bianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chuyin had been a dashing commander in whom the troops placed their hope; with his death they lost all will to fight, and Guangyuan escaped and fled back to Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，思明陷魏州，所殺三萬人。

translations.literal: On day dingmao, Siming took Weizhou and killed thirty thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao, Shi Siming captured Weizhou and slaughtered thirty thousand people.

sentences.zh: 平盧節度使王玄志薨，上遣中使往撫慰將士，且就察軍中所欲立者，授以旌節。

translations.literal: Pinglu military commissioner Wang Xuanzhi died; the emperor sent a palace envoy to comfort the troops and also to observe whom the army wished to establish, and grant him the banner and tally.
translations.idiomatic: Pinglu military commissioner Wang Xuanzhi died. The emperor sent a palace envoy to comfort the troops and to learn whom the army wished to install, then invest that man with the commissioner's banner and tally.

sentences.zh: 高麗人李懷玉為裨將，殺玄志之子，推侯希逸為平盧軍使。

translations.literal: The Koguryo man Li Huaiyu was a deputy general; he killed Xuanzhi's son and pushed Hou Xiyi to be Pinglu army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Li Huaiyu, a Koguryo officer serving as deputy general, killed Xuanzhi's son and installed Hou Xiyi as commander of the Pinglu army.

sentences.zh: 希逸之母，懷玉姑也，故懷玉立之。

translations.literal: Xiyi's mother was Huaiyu's paternal aunt, therefore Huaiyu established him.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Xiyi's mother was Li Huaiyu's aunt, which was why Huaiyu chose him.

sentences.zh: 朝廷因以希逸為節度副使。

translations.literal: The court accordingly made Xiyi deputy military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court then appointed Hou Xiyi deputy military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 節度使由軍士廢立自此始。

translations.literal: Military commissioners deposed and established by the troops began from this.
translations.idiomatic: From this point military commissioners began to be deposed and installed by their own troops.

sentences.zh: 臣光曰：夫民生有欲，無主則亂。

translations.literal: Your servant Guang says: The people by nature have desires; without a ruler there is disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remarks: Human beings are born with desires; without a ruler, chaos follows.

sentences.zh: 是故聖人制禮以治之。

translations.literal: Therefore the sages instituted ritual to govern them.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sages established ritual to govern them.

sentences.zh: 自天子、諸侯至於卿、大夫、士、庶人，尊卑有分，大小有倫，若綱條之相維，臂指之相使，是以民服事其上，而下無覬覦。

translations.literal: From the Son of Heaven and feudal lords down to ministers, grand masters, officers, and commoners, there were distinctions of honor and patterns of precedence and subordination, like cords of a net supporting one another and arm and fingers commanding one another—thereby the people served those above and those below had no covetous glances.
translations.idiomatic: From the Son of Heaven and feudal lords down through ministers, grand masters, officers, and commoners, honor and subordination were fixed in their places, great and small ranked in proper order—like the strands of a net holding one another or arm and fingers working together—so that the people served those above and no one below cast covetous eyes upward.

sentences.zh: 其在《周易》，「上天、下澤，履。

translations.literal: In the Book of Changes it is said: "Heaven above, the Marsh below—Treading (Lü).
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Heaven above, the Marsh below: Treading (Lü)."

sentences.zh: 」象曰：「君子以辨上下，定民志。

translations.literal: " The Image says: "The noble man distinguishes above and below and settles the people's aspirations.
translations.idiomatic: The Image says: "The noble man distinguishes above from below and settles the people's will."

sentences.zh: 」此之謂也。

translations.literal: " This is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: That is the meaning.

sentences.zh: 凡人君所以能有其臣民者，以八柄存乎己也。

translations.literal: The reason an ordinary ruler can possess his ministers and people is that the eight handles reside in himself.
translations.idiomatic: A ruler can command ministers and people only because the eight handles of power rest in his own hands.

sentences.zh: 苟或捨之，則彼此之勢均，何以使其下哉！

translations.literal: If he casts them away, then the power of each side is equal—how can he command those below!
translations.idiomatic: If he relinquishes them, ruler and ruled stand on equal footing—how then can he command those below?

sentences.zh: 肅宗遭唐中衰，幸而復國，是宜正上下之禮以綱紀四方；

translations.literal: Suzong encountered the mid-decline of Tang and by good fortune restored the state; he ought to have rectified the ritual of above and below to bind and order the four quarters;
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Suzong lived through the Tang dynasty's mid-reign collapse and by fortune restored the realm; he should have restored proper ritual between superior and subordinate to bring discipline to the four quarters;

sentences.zh: 而偷取一時之安，不思永久之患。

translations.literal: yet he stole a moment's peace and did not think of lasting calamity.
translations.idiomatic: yet he grasped at immediate peace and gave no thought to lasting ruin.

sentences.zh: 彼命將帥，統籓維，國之大事也，乃委一介之使，徇行伍之情，無問賢不肖，惟其所欲與者則授之。

translations.literal: Appointing generals and commanders and governing the frontier pillars were great affairs of state, yet he entrusted a single envoy, indulging the feelings of the ranks, asking neither worthy nor unworthy, and granting office only to whomever they wished.
translations.idiomatic: Appointing generals and governing the frontier circuits was a matter of supreme state importance, yet he left it to a single palace envoy who indulged the troops' wishes, never asking whether a man was worthy, but investing whoever they wanted.

sentences.zh: 自是之後，積習為常，君臣循守，以為得策，謂之姑息。

translations.literal: From this time forward, accumulated practice became custom; ruler and minister circled and guarded it, thinking it a winning policy—they called it indulgent appeasement.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the practice hardened into custom; emperors and ministers clung to it as sound policy and called it indulgent appeasement.

sentences.zh: 乃至偏裨士卒，殺逐主帥，亦不治其罪，因以其位任授之。

translations.literal: So far as to reach that deputy officers and common soldiers killed and expelled their commanders, yet they were not punished for their crime, but instead were granted that office and post.
translations.idiomatic: It went so far that junior officers and common soldiers who killed or drove out their commanders went unpunished and were given the dead man's rank and command.

sentences.zh: 然則爵祿、廢置、殺生、予奪皆不出於上而出於下，亂之生也，庸有極乎！

translations.literal: Then ranks and stipends, appointment and dismissal, killing and granting life, giving and taking away—all did not issue from above but from below. Could disorder born of this have any limit!
translations.idiomatic: Thus rank and stipend, appointment and dismissal, life and death, reward and punishment—all ceased to issue from the throne and issued instead from the ranks below. Was there any limit to the disorder such a system could breed?

sentences.zh: 且夫有國家者，賞善而誅惡，故為善者勸，為惡者懲。

translations.literal: Moreover, one who possesses a state rewards the good and punishes the evil, so that those who do good are encouraged and those who do evil are chastised.
translations.idiomatic: Every state rewards the good and punishes the wicked, encouraging virtue and chastening crime.

sentences.zh: 彼為人下而殺逐其上，惡孰大焉！

translations.literal: Those who as inferiors kill and expel their superiors—what evil could be greater!
translations.idiomatic: For subordinates to kill or drive out their superiors—what crime could be greater?

sentences.zh: 乃使之擁旄秉鉞，師長一方，是賞之也。

translations.literal: Yet they were made to bear the banner and wield the battle-axe, commanding a region—it was rewarding them.
translations.idiomatic: Yet such men were allowed to bear the commissioner's banner and battle-axe and govern whole circuits—as if they were being rewarded.

sentences.zh: 賞以勸惡，惡其何所不至乎！

translations.literal: Rewarding to encourage evil—how far could evil not reach!
translations.idiomatic: To reward crime is to invite it—what wickedness would not follow?

sentences.zh: 《書》云：「遠乃猷。

translations.literal: The Book of Documents says: "Keep your plans far-reaching.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Documents says: "Keep your plans far-sighted."

sentences.zh: 」《詩》云：「猷之未遠，是用大諫。

translations.literal: " The Book of Odes says: "Since the plans are not far-reaching, therefore a great remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Odes says: "Because your counsel is not far-sighted, a stern rebuke is required."

sentences.zh: 」孔子曰：「人無遠慮，必有近憂。

translations.literal: " Confucius said: "One without far-reaching consideration is sure to have near worries.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: "He who lacks foresight will soon face trouble at hand."

sentences.zh: 」為天下之政，而專事姑息，其憂患可勝校乎！

translations.literal: " Governing all under Heaven yet devoting oneself solely to indulgent appeasement—can its troubles and disasters be counted!
translations.idiomatic: To govern the empire yet devote oneself entirely to appeasement—is it possible even to count the disasters that will follow?

sentences.zh: 由是為下者常眄眄焉伺其上，苟得間則攻而族之；

translations.literal: Hence inferiors constantly cast sidelong glances watching those above; if they gain an opening they attack and exterminate them to the last;
translations.idiomatic: Hence subordinates constantly watch their superiors with sidelong eyes, ready at the first opening to strike and wipe out their entire families;

sentences.zh: 為上者常惴惴焉畏其下，苟得間則掩而屠之；

translations.literal: superiors constantly fear those below in trepidation; if they gain an opening they ambush and slaughter them;
translations.idiomatic: while superiors live in constant dread of those below and, given the chance, strike first to slaughter them;

sentences.zh: 爭務先發以逞其志，非有相保養為俱利久存之計也。

translations.literal: each striving to strike first to vent his will—not having plans to protect and nourish one another for mutual profit and long survival.
translations.idiomatic: each side rushes to strike first and satisfy its will, with no thought of mutual protection or a shared interest in lasting survival.

sentences.zh: 如是而求天下之安，其可得乎！

translations.literal: Seeking the peace of all under Heaven in such a way—can it be obtained!
translations.idiomatic: To seek peace under Heaven in such a world—is it possible?

sentences.zh: 跡其厲階，肇於此矣。

translations.literal: Tracing the stages of ruin, it began from this.
translations.idiomatic: Trace the steps of ruin to their source, and they begin here.

sentences.zh: 蓋古者治軍必本於禮，故晉文公城濮之戰，見其師少長有禮，知其可用。

translations.literal: For in antiquity governing the army always took ritual as its root; therefore at Duke Wen of Jin's battle of Chengpu, when he saw their army's young and old observing ritual, he knew they could be used.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity, governing an army always rested on ritual. At Duke Wen of Jin's battle of Chengpu, when he saw young and old in the enemy ranks observing proper ceremony, he knew that army could be put to use.

sentences.zh: 今唐治軍而不顧禮，使士卒得以陵偏裨，偏裨得以陵將帥，則將帥之陵天子，自然之勢也。

translations.literal: Now Tang governs the army without regard to ritual, letting soldiers override deputy officers and deputy officers override commanders—then commanders overriding the Son of Heaven is the natural tendency.
translations.idiomatic: Tang now governed its armies without regard to ritual, allowing soldiers to dominate their officers, officers their commanders—and commanders dominating the Son of Heaven was the natural next step.

sentences.zh: 由是禍亂繼起，兵革不息，民墜塗炭，無所控訴，凡二百餘年。

translations.literal: From this disaster and disorder arose in succession, weapons and armor never ceased, the people fell into charcoal and paste with nowhere to appeal, altogether more than two hundred years.
translations.idiomatic: Disaster followed disaster; war never ceased; the people were ground to ash with nowhere to plead for justice—for more than two hundred years.

sentences.zh: 然後宋受命。

translations.literal: Only then did Song receive the Mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Only then did the Song receive Heaven's mandate.

sentences.zh: 太祖始制軍法，使以階級相承，小有違犯，鹹伏斧質。

translations.literal: Taizu first instituted military law, making ranks succeed one by another in order; the slightest violation—all submitted to the axe.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu first codified military law so that ranks succeeded one another in strict order and even minor violations brought the executioner's block.

sentences.zh: 是以上下有敘，令行禁止，四征不庭，無思不服，宇內乂安，兆民允殖，以迄於今，皆由治軍以禮故也。

translations.literal: Therefore above and below had order, orders were carried out and prohibitions enforced, on four sides they punished those who did not attend court, none who thought of it failed to submit, within the four seas there was order and peace, the myriad people were truly nourished—down to the present, all because of governing the army through ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Hence superior and subordinate were ordered, commands ran and prohibitions held, rebels were punished on every frontier until none dared refuse submission, the realm was pacified, and the people flourished—down to the present day, all because armies were governed through ritual.

sentences.zh: 豈非詒謀之遠哉！

translations.literal: Is this not far-reaching counsel passed down!
translations.idiomatic: Was this not foresight of extraordinary reach!

sentences.zh: 是歲，置振武節度使，領鎮北大都護府、麟、勝二州；

translations.literal: In this year the Zhenwu military commissioner was established, overseeing the Great Protectorate-General of the Pacified North and the two prefectures Lin and Sheng;
translations.idiomatic: That year the court established the Zhenwu military commission, governing the Great Protectorate-General of the Pacified North and the prefectures of Lin and Sheng;

sentences.zh: 又置陝虢華及豫許汝二節度使。

translations.literal: and also established the two military commissions of Shan-Guo-Hua and Yu-Xu-Ru.
translations.idiomatic: and also created the Shan-Guo-Hua and Yu-Xu-Ru military commissions.

sentences.zh: 安南經略使為節度使，領交、陸等十一州。

translations.literal: The Annan pacification commissioner became military commissioner, overseeing Jiao, Lu, and eleven other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: The Annan pacification commissioner was elevated to military commissioner, governing Jiao, Lu, and eleven other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃陷河源軍。

translations.literal: Tibet took Heyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: The Tibetans captured Heyuan Army.
